body: **Chunk:** `2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci` · viola-0.1.0 · Epoch 7 — Cross-OS completion (its third and last entry)

**The working entry:** Linux-only code and CI — no Windows or macOS code, tests, fixtures or CI jobs left, recoverable at
a pushed tag; every gate green on Linux.

- **The tag comes first.** `multi-os-final` is set on the last commit that still holds the three-OS code and pushed to
  origin before any removal commit, so every removed line can be recovered (the founder's second answer, 2026-11-04 21:50Z,
  «Вырезать, с тегом»; the first CARRY; the operator's directive, item 2). Re-read at take-up: no tag `multi-os-*` stands,
  locally or on origin.

- **Removed:** every `cfg(windows)` and `cfg(target_os = "macos")` arm with its tests and fixtures; the four
  Windows-only files `src/conpty.rs` (92 lines), `crates/viola-pty/src/sideload.rs` (243), `tests/conpty_sideload.rs` (386)
  and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` (425), 1 146 lines re-read at take-up; `vendor/conpty/`; the
  `[target.'cfg(windows)']` dependencies in `Cargo.toml` and the crates' manifests, with their `deny.toml` entries (the
  first CARRY). Each named path stands at HEAD, re-read at take-up.

- **Removed from CI:** the Windows and macOS jobs of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (test, lint, perf, release),
  `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`'s Windows and macOS jobs, and `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` as a whole; any
  pre-push or harness step that runs only for those OSes (the first CARRY).
- **Made unconditional:** a `cfg(unix)` arm whose only sibling was removed loses its gate (the first CARRY).

- **The census of OS-gated tests** from «Linux and macOS parity», `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs`, is re-pointed or
  retired along with the gates it counted (the first CARRY).

- [inferred] `scripts/agent-run.ps1` is the PowerShell twin of the harness, and only Windows CI steps run it (re-read at
  take-up: `ci.yml`'s two `pwsh shim` steps and `windows-mutants.yml`'s mutants step). Whether it is "a harness step that
  runs only for those OSes", and so leaves with them, is P3's to read and P4's to decide. CLAUDE.md, the harness letters
  and the new-session health check 13 name the `{sh,ps1}` pair.

- [inferred] Text that names Windows or macOS without a `cfg` gate (doc comments, help strings, the `.cmd` / `.bat`
  refusal, the closed words `conpty-sideload` · `conpty` · `sideload_fallback`, `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` and the macOS
  carve-out, the schemas' OS words) is in scope only where the removal leaves it naming code that no longer exists. P3
  lists it, and P4 decides each one against the masters' change below.

- [inferred] The removal changes no Linux behaviour: every Linux code path, closed word, exit code and wire contract
  stays as it is, and only the other OSes' arms leave.

- CARRY (the founder's ruling of 2026-11-04, live, 21:43Z; his second answer at 21:50Z «Вырезать, с тегом»): relayed by
  the Viola overseer in the snapshot `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-04T23-11-43-wrap/inputs/I2-restructure-linux-only.md.txt`,
  item 3. The entry was placed first by the operator's directive
  (`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-04T23-11-43-wrap/inputs/I1-wrap-linux-only-directive.md.txt`, item 1) and by the overseer's
  technical answer, founder-delegated (`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-04T23-11-43-wrap/inputs/I3-relay-1.md.txt`, Q3). Its
  content is folded into «What it builds» above. All three paths stand at HEAD, re-read at take-up.

- CARRY (its acceptance, the same snapshot, item 3): every gate green on Linux; no Windows or macOS job in any workflow;
  no `cfg(windows)` or `target_os = "macos"` left in the tree; the tag `multi-os-final` resolves on origin.

- [inferred] That CARRY's measured hypotheses, their markers kept verbatim: "Hypotheses to re-read at take-up, measured
  by this wrap at HEAD `abf00915`: the pattern `cfg!?\(.*(windows|target_os = "macos")` over `git ls-files '*.rs'`
  matches 274 lines in 64 files (96 185 `.rs` lines in all); the four named Windows-only files hold 1 146 lines; no tag
  `multi-os-final` stands. The relay's own reading at `28bbddab` was 224 gates in 55 files of about 67k Rust lines, its
  pattern unnamed". Re-read at take-up: 1 146 lines, no tag. The pattern count is P3's to measure.

- [inferred] CARRY (the same snapshot, item 6, the overseer's measurement), its claim kept verbatim: "the `msrv` job
  126926985207 of ci#41930831242 on `abf00915` (the wrap commit of «Linux and macOS parity») failed two `viola-e2e`
  harness unit cases, `e2e_home_backing_gone_target_is_made_again_owner_only` and
  `e2e_home_backing_owner_only_target_is_kept_untouched`, each panicking `e2e-home backing: 7233 MiB free, below the 9216
  MiB floor` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs:483`), 2669 passed and 2 failed; the diff under test touched no harness
  code; the overseer's reading is that the cases read the runner's real free space against the floor, so they pass or
  fail by the host's disk". Re-read at take-up: the two cases stand at `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs:481` and

  cases decide on a free-space figure the test controls, never the host's, and `msrv` is green. P3 closes the mechanism
  against that run.

- CARRY (the masters change here, once, with the code; the same snapshot, item 5; the wrap's dialog, the overseer's
  technical answer, founder-delegated, 2026-11-05 06:00Z, recorded in

  - test-plan: the 3-OS CI matrix, the per-OS legs;
  - security-plan: its Windows ACL and named-pipe sections stay, as the unsupported OS's text;

- No Linux behaviour moves: no new exit code (the typed set stays 0, 1, 2, 10–14, 20, 21), no wire contract or closed word

- No env, flag or feature seam forces a refusing peer-euid decision (CLAUDE.md's invariant).

- Everything carried here is the founder's own ruling, and his go for this chunk is his word of 2026-11-05, relayed by

body:
# Phase directive — "Linux-only code and CI" (Epoch 7's last entry)

The operator's requests to the phase's orchestrator (the overseer, founder-delegated).

1. **The founder's rulings this entry carries are his own, live** (2026-11-04 21:43Z, 21:50Z and 21:53Z: Linux only;
   remove the Windows and macOS code after a tag; the core on any current Linux, CI on `ubuntu-latest`). His go for this
   chunk is his word of 2026-11-05, relayed by overseer1. The entry's CARRYs hold the scope, the removal list and the
   acceptance. Plan to them.
2. **The tag comes first.** `multi-os-final` goes on the last commit that still holds the three-OS code, and is pushed
   to origin before any removal commit. Its resolving on origin is part of the acceptance.
3. **The sampler stays unforced.** Keep every subagent and Workflow transcript, and leave the run dir intact.
4. **A dead draw follows the contract.** It takes the contract's one re-spawn, and then the contract decides; only
   `every draw dead` stops. Stop and report, with the run dir, at any other hard cascade failure.
5. **A tool fault stops the phase.** If an Andromeda tool crashes, refuses wrongly or contradicts its letter, stop at once,
   report it with the run dir, and patch nothing.
6. **Live sessions: 0 for this chunk** unless the founder gives a number. Everything runs on the fake agent. A
   boundary widening or a route split is his live word: ask it as a P4 dialog, and keep the questions he alone answers
   separate from the technical ones.
7. **Standing:** read `df -h /tmp` before a stamped-home gate. Epoch 6's diagnosis and audit run ONCE at the version end
   by the founder's word, so leave new-session's nudge unanswered.
8. **Since the last chunk:** agents' outputs are field-form only (an old-grammar payload is refused). The masters and
   the harness live in the store (`rec.py read` · `tree` · `find` · `get`; curation by `rec.py harness land`). Follow
   the letters over any habit.
9. **HEAD is one local commit ahead of origin** (`ecbe7ab3`, overseer1's one-time store pass). It goes out with this
   chunk's pushes.
10. **On the P5 card:** every refusal, with the letter line you were following, and P5's `landed tx` line.

body: - **Depth:** deep · **Reads:** 19 · **Globs/Greps:** 24

- **Harness rules consulted:** `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` — read whole (auto-loaded in this window, its
  `## Session Additions` included); no live leg in this chunk (0 live sessions, `inputs#I1` item 6), so no firing form
  is taken from it beyond the harness verbs the gates name.

- **Platform issues consulted:** `gh issue view 14405 --repo actions/runner-images` → the maintainers state "the
  guaranteed free disk space for Ubuntu runners is 14 GB" (closed 2026-07-17; a `df -h` there reads 16G available on
  `/`); `gh issue view 14777 --repo actions/runner-images` → on ubuntu-26.04 `/tmp` is a tmpfs at 50 % of RAM (~7.8G)
  with `usrquota`, open; `gh pr view 14814 --repo actions/runner-images` → "[Ubuntu 26.04] Keep /tmp on the root disk",
  MERGED 2026-10-20. The red msrv job ran on `Image: ubuntu-24.04, Version: 20261101.114.1` (its log, line 17-18), where
  `/tmp` is on the root disk, so the 26.04 tmpfs is not this run's cause; the run read 7233 MiB free on the backing's
  filesystem after its own build.

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` — the operator's directive for this phase (tag first and pushed before any removal;
  0 live sessions; a tool fault stops; the P5 card's contents).

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs` (85-160, 440-540) — `ensure_e2e_home` reads `free_bytes(&target)` (statvfs) of
  the linked backing and refuses through `headroom_refusal(free, HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB)` (line 120); the two msrv cases
  build a backing under `tempfile::tempdir()` and call it, so the runner's free space decides them.

- `crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs` (120-175) — `SERVER_PID_REPORTED = cfg!(not(target_os = "macos"))` (136),
  `server_pid_of` per OS, `PEER_EUID_REPORTED = cfg!(unix)` (149), `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)`.

- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` (131-153) — `server_verdict(…, peer_pid_reported)`: `false` returns `Matches`
  with no comparison (138-139), the macOS carve-out; with `true` a missing pid or start is `Unverifiable`.

- `crates/viola-state/src/fs.rs` (248-300) — `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS`, `HOST_IS_WINDOWS = cfg!(windows)`, `retry_replace`,
  `replace_private_retrying`: the replace retry is a Windows-only decision; on Linux `retry_replace` never holds.

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` (207-256, 400-545) — `Search { windows }`, `HOST_IS_WINDOWS = cfg!(windows)`,
  `resolve_program` returns at `!search.windows || !is_script(…)`; `BatchScriptChild` is produced only on the Windows
  arm, and `resolve_program_on_unix_takes_the_bare_name_and_never_refuses` pins that Unix never refuses.

- `src/run/mod.rs` (140-152) — the product resolver reads `PATH` and `PATHEXT` unconditionally and passes
  `Search::HOST_IS_WINDOWS`.

- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs` (18-30) — `#[cfg(windows)] mod sideload;`, `pty_backend()` words `conpty-sideload` ·
  `conpty` · `openpty`.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/host.rs` (370-690) and `scratch.rs` (11-350) — the host-exclusion reader

- **CI jobs by OS** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `test`, `perf`, `lint`, `release` run a matrix `[windows-2025,

- **A Windows-only module per file**: `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs:535` `#[cfg(windows)] mod win;` →

- **The msrv mechanism** (re-derived at HEAD and against the run): the two cases' backing lies under the runner's

- **No Linux path changes when the Windows arms leave**: `resolve_program` already returns before the script check

- **Precedents in the sidecars**: the 2026-10-16 browser-leg removal took its closed words, its deny ban and its probe

- **Workflow hygiene** (security-plan §Dependency Security): `permissions: {}`, job `contents: read`, SHA-pinned

# P4 dialog — the closed words that lose their only emitter

Asked at phase P4 of chunk 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci, one question, technical.

## The question, as asked

The Windows and macOS code goes, but some closed words only that code emitted would stay in the wire contracts and
schemas: `batch-script-child` (revive --json and verify codes, the process-exit detail enum,
AgentError::BatchScriptChild), `sideload_fallback` with its five words on process-start, and `os`'s `windows` ·
`macos` in schemas/diag-line.v1.json. Linux never emits any of them today (resolve_program never refuses on Unix). Do
they leave with the code, or stay as reserved words with no emitter?

1. Remove with the code (Recommended) — each word leaves its schema enum, closed code list and pinned test literal in
   the same change, and the wrap's obs/arch amendments record the removal (the 2026-10-16 browser-leg precedent).
2. Keep as reserved, no emitter — the schemas and closed lists stay byte-identical; only the code that produced the
   words goes (the 2026-10-16T14-58-10-wrap precedent).

## The answer, verbatim

Chosen: «Remove with the code (Recommended)».

Notes: «The overseer, technical answer (founder-delegated), 2026-11-05 11:08Z, within the founder's own ruling of
2026-11-04 21:50Z (remove the Windows and macOS code, recoverable at the tag): a closed word no build can emit leaves
with its emitter. The scope's «no closed word changes» boundary is narrowed to these words by this answer; record it
so.»

## Authority

delegate the Viola overseer, 2026-11-05 11:08Z (a technical answer, founder-delegated), resting on the founder's own
ruling of 2026-11-04 21:50Z. A narrowing, no boundary widening: no escalate pattern of the playbook names it.

   - `test_support`'s `canonical_sddl`, `dacl_of` and `user_sid` leave.
   - `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` leave, their Linux value folded in:
     - `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own)` is `observed == Some(own)`, still proven over injected values, with no env,
       flag or feature seam (security-plan/security-anti-patterns fct-lvhmwli7). A peer whose euid cannot be read stays
       refused.
     - `peer_admitted(observed)` and `serve_admitting` keep their roles.
   - `lib.rs`'s re-exports follow.

5. **viola-state**.
   - `liveness.rs`: `server_verdict` and `verify_server` lose the `peer_pid_reported` parameter and its macOS `Matches`
     arm (`liveness.rs:138-139`). With a pid always reported, the verdict reads today's Linux path (research Patterns
     detected). `server_verdict_rows` loses its no-pid row and keeps every Linux row.
   - `strict.rs`: the Windows owner/DACL arm, `windows_read_verdict`, `READ_RIGHTS` and the `win` tests leave.
     `check_socket_dir`'s off-Unix `Ok(())` arm leaves and its Unix body is made unconditional. Its `NotADirectory`,
     `Symlink` and `Unreadable` verdicts stay exact, and no check-free `Ok(())` arm remains (security-plan
     fct-fmxdaj54).
   - `fs.rs`: `HOST_IS_WINDOWS`, `retry_replace`, `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS`, `replace_private_retrying` and their unit cases
     leave, so `replace_private` makes one attempt as it does on Linux today. `create_private_dir`'s DACL arm leaves.
     `replace_private_shared` stays for the plugin files.
   - `pin.rs`: `pin_companions`, the companions' held open and their `retry_open` / `open_held_waiting` leave.
     `pin_bytes` and the pinned copy's re-hash stay (security-plan/data-protection fct-i5etdjvh). A `PinError` variant
     left with no producer leaves.
   - `snapshot.rs`, `board.rs`: their OS arms leave. `board_scan`'s Linux read rule stays.

6. **viola-agent-claude** (`lib.rs`, `statusline.rs`, `ledger.rs`).
   - `resolve_program` loses `Search::windows`, `pathext`, `HOST_IS_WINDOWS`, `is_script`, `SHIM_TARGET` and
     `AgentError::BatchScriptChild` (`inputs#I2`). It resolves a given path as given and a bare name on `PATH`, as
     `resolve_program_on_unix_takes_the_bare_name_and_never_refuses` pins today. `ProgramNotFound` keeps its fixed
     message.
   - `WRAPPED_HERE` leaves, its `true` folded in: the override, probe and shell-argv builders take the wrapped path,
     and `LedgerRow::relied()` is all twenty-four rows.
   - The unit cases of the removed arms leave, and every Linux case stays.

7. **viola-mcp** (`crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`, `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs`): the `SERVER_PID_REPORTED`
   argument leaves. `handlers.rs`'s macOS gates are made unconditional and keep every Linux assertion.

8. **The root bin.**
   - `src/conpty.rs` is deleted.
   - `src/main.rs`: `restrict_dll_search` and the sideload pre-load leave. The panic hook stays `main`'s first
     statement.
   - `src/cmd/run.rs`: the `run.conpty_sideload` step, `pin_companions`, `sideload_fallback` and the `BatchScriptChild`
     arm of the start's refusals leave. The start's remaining order and every other refusal stay.
   - `src/cmd/verify.rs`: its `BatchScriptChild` arm and the Windows relied count leave.
   - `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`: the console-control arm leaves; `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` are made unconditional.
   - `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs`: the `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` argument leaves.
   - The macOS gates of `refused_inside` and the `last.rs` / `pause.rs` / `unlink.rs` / `link.rs` / `send.rs` /
     `wait.rs` / `release.rs` / `answer.rs` test modules leave, so every captured-span case runs on Linux.
   - `src/run/env.rs`: the registry reader and the case-insensitive match leave. The exact strip, `claude_env_keep`
     and the eleven-name identity floor stay (security-plan/secret-management fct-fdqq3i6o).
   - `src/run/mod.rs`: `PATHEXT` and `Search::HOST_IS_WINDOWS` leave, and `sideload_fallback` leaves `log_child_start`.
   - `src/run/version_gate.rs`, `src/panic_frames.rs` (the Unix capture becomes the one path, the same line shape),
     `src/human/style.rs` (VT enable: decision rungs 1–6 and the depth choice unchanged, design-system fct-gu2srphh),
     `src/human/verbs.rs` and `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`: their OS arms leave or are made unconditional.
   - The Git Bash rewritten-path warning (`src/cmd/send.rs:60`) runs on every OS today and stays.

9. **The closed words that leave** (`inputs#I2`).
   - `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`: `os` reads `["linux"]`, the `sideload_fallback` property leaves `process-start`, and
     `batch-script-child` leaves the `process-exit` `detail` enum. Its count is re-measured by its rule (the enum's
     members), never copied (obs history n=52).
   - revive's and verify's closed code lists and the `.cmd`/`.bat` human pair leave with the variant.
   - Each pinned literal moves in the same commit: `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` `CAUSES` and its top comment,
     `tests/cli_revive.rs`, `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`, `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`.
   - The `thiserror::Error` census (`command grep -rn "thiserror::Error" src crates --include=*.rs`) and the
     `human::refuse` census (`grep -rcE 'human::refuse\(' src`) are re-measured by their rules (keeps design S1, S2).

10. **viola-e2e harness.**
    - `harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs`: `HOST_SCRATCH` and the Windows scratch wipe leave; off Windows the arm was
      inert, so Linux behaviour is unchanged.
    - `harness/run/mutants.rs`: its call sites follow.
    - `harness/run/mutants/host.rs`: the host family is Linux's. Its planted fixture sources are re-planted on a
      predicate that is false on Linux and names neither `windows` nor `macos` (for example `target_os = "freebsd"`),
      so the reader's cases keep their verdicts.
    - `harness/cleanup.rs`: the Windows pipe arm of `endpoint_gone` leaves and the Unix `unconnectable` reading is made
      unconditional.
    - `harness/secret_scan.rs`: its OS arm leaves.
    - `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`: its OS gate leaves.

11. **The Windows-only test files leave whole**: `tests/conpty_sideload.rs`, `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs`,
    `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs`, `tests/cli_program_resolution.rs` and `tests/security_negatives_channel.rs`.

12. **The tests' arms and support** (every remaining file of research's list under `tests/`, plus
    `crates/viola-channel/tests/channel_frames.rs`).
    - Each `cfg(windows)` / `target_os = "macos"` arm leaves, and each `cfg(unix)` whose only sibling left is made
      unconditional, its Linux assertion word for word.
    - `tests/support/home.rs` loses `seed_conpty`, the `icacls` arms of `widen` · `grant_read` · `unwiden` ·
      `still_widened` and the `USERPROFILE` arm. `SOCKET_ROOT_VAR` reads `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.
    - `tests/support/frozen.rs` keeps the Unix `kill -STOP` twin only, ungated.
    - `tests/run_cli.rs` keeps `kill -KILL` only.
    - `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` loses its `#![cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`.
    - `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs`'s hangup case loses its `cfg(target_os = "linux")` gate (its `ps -o sigignore=` reader
      stays).
    - `tests/cli_verify.rs`'s Windows literals leave; the 24-row Unix literals stay, ungated.
    - Every endpoint directory an edited impostor, fail-open or handler test makes stays `create_private_dir` (test-plan
      §8). No case becomes `#[ignore]` (keeps tests S2–S4, S8; a11y S1–S3).

13. **The census re-pointed** (`tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs`).
    - `GATES` holds exactly the gates that remain, under `tests/` and `crates/*/tests/`.
    - A gate whose predicate names `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` reads as a fault even when a row names it, so the
      Linux-only tree is a standing check.
    - The planted self-check case at line 684 is re-planted so each fault class still fires.
    - It stays a root `contract_` binary in `nextest-e2e` (test-plan/test-strategy fct-df3r2j7c).

14. **CI, scripts and repository rules.**
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
      - `test`, `perf`, `lint` and `release` keep `strategy.matrix.os: [ubuntu-latest]`, so every job name and every
        `diag-`, `harness-`, `junit-`, `perf-`, `diag-perf-` and `secret-scan-` artifact keeps its `${{ matrix.os }}`
        form (obs S1, S2; security S1, S2).
      - The `ConPTY vendor verification` step and both `pwsh shim` steps leave. The `sh shim` steps and `Lint probes`
        lose their `if: runner.os` conditions.
      - Every other step, order, pin, `permissions: {}` / `contents: read`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` and the `test`-job
        `tool:` line stay (tests S5–S7).
    - `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml` is deleted. `nightly.yml` is unchanged (two ubuntu jobs).
    - `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh`, `scripts/junit-os-sets.py` and `scripts/agent-run.ps1` are deleted (leaned below).
    - `scripts/agent-run.sh` loses its `.ps1`/three-OS comment.
    - `scripts/orphans-check.sh`: its triples narrow to `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. Its `--probe` control is re-planted
      so it still reads `orphans-check probes: 2/2 fired, control clean` with one triple.
    - `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` loses its darwin and windows asset arms. `scripts/lint-probes.sh` and
      `scripts/release-check.sh` lose their Windows comments.
    - `.gitattributes` loses `vendor/conpty/** binary`, and `vendor/conpty/` is deleted.
    - `.config/nextest.toml:24` loses `binary(conpty_sideload)` (the `binary(…)` names 27 → 26 by that rule).

15. **The bounded-readers census** (`tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`): each `BOUNDARIES` / `EXCEPTIONS` needle whose
    line the removal edits is re-pointed at the line that stands, and its stands-check stays green
    (security-plan/input-validation fct-jy3jkgu2).
- none — the removal adds no file

- research `## Files to modify` (105 items, `doc:2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci/research`), each with its change;
  the deletions are listed there.

No live leg: nothing drives the real `claude` (`inputs#I1` item 6). The stamped-home entries read `df -h /tmp` first
(`inputs#I1` item 7). There is no mutation entry (the epoch-boundary audit owns `run --mutants`; testing.md 2026-10-04).
The diff is OS-sensitive by construction: every `cfg(windows)` / macOS arm leaves and `cfg(unix)` gates leave. So the tag,
hygiene, push and CI entries close the block, and the CI read names the one leg left. The msrv job's own form
(`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96`) runs locally too: the dev host holds the 1.96 toolchain (`rustup toolchain list`).

  pushed sha's CI run on `ubuntu-latest` reads `verdict: green`, `msrv` included, with every job and artifact name intact

  fixed refusal, `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` is one unchanged compiled constant, and the `msrv` job is green

  `windows`/`macos` predicate reading as a fault, and its self-check firing on every planted class

  `channel-tokio-free.sh`, `deny-probes.sh` (every ban fired, control clean), `zizmor`, `rmcp-features.sh` and
  `release-check.sh --probe` (5/5 refused) each pass on Linux (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (security) On Linux the socket-directory, peer-euid and server-identity refusals and the strict-modes check read as
  before, with no check-free `Ok(())` arm and no seam forcing a refusing peer-euid decision. The un-gated negatives

  `[DIM, BOLD, RESET, DIM, RESET]` witness, the `HELP` and `CAPTION` literals, and every Linux `unable` / `hint:` pair

Asked at phase P5 step 1 of chunk 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci (a red on an existing property, its owner named
before approval; a contestable fork returns to P4's form), one question, technical.

P5's baseline of `cargo deny --format json check` reads red on the untouched tree: RUSTSEC-2026-0441 (`pin-utils` is
unmaintained, dated 2026-10-01), reached only through the pinned `portable-pty =0.8.1` → `nix 0.25.1`. It's a Linux path
and external decay, not this chunk's subject, and CI's supply-chain job will read it red on this chunk's push. The rules
forbid widening the one ignore to reach green. Who owns this red?

(`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96`) runs locally too: the dev host holds the 1.96 toolchain (`rustup toolchain list`).

(`inputs#I3`), with no ignore widened. So `cargo deny check advisories` and the supply-chain read are report-only
(`expect = []`), and every other job is asserted green. supply-chain's later steps do not run in CI after its deny
step fails, so their local entries are their reading. The secret scan is not listed: `agent-run.sh secret-scan` ran

If a listed command's post-condition is "none" or not yet measured on this CLI version (`/remote-control` today), the send returns `ok` with `{"confirmed":false,"detail":"unconfirmable"}`. Nothing else is ever unconfirmable. Any other unconfirmed send is `not-delivered`. The decision depends on the ledger, never on a leading slash. The local-command list and the `/clear` row are compiled (`viola_agent_claude::ledger::LOCAL_COMMANDS`: `/clear` with the post-condition "a new session", `/remote-control` with none, `/compact` with "a SessionStart with source `compact` and the session's own `session_id`" (`PostCondition::CompactedSession`; listed since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows on the founder's own answer to its P4 fork 1, relayed verbatim by the operator; row `local-command-compact`); row `local-command-clear`, stamped on 2.1.287 by chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows through the ratified typed-input probe), and `send` consumes them (as landed by chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes; the decision is `classify` in `src/run/send/classify.rs`). - **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs, so no file is both appended to and exclusively locked (that pair fails on Windows, rust-lang/rust#54118). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

- **[Snapshot writer] tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` and `persist_noclobber` through the shared helpers of `viola_state::fs`.** `viola_state::fs::replace_private` creates the temp file beside the target, sets its mode before any byte is written (0600), writes, `sync_all`s and `persist`s; a failure leaves the target as it was. `replace_private` is one attempt: a failed `persist` returns at once, the target as it was; `write_snapshot` calls it. `replace_private_shared` is the variant for files every concurrent start of one version writes identically (the plugin files): a replace that fails counts as done when the target already holds exactly those bytes. The pinned copy's absent-copy write is never a replace: it is the no-clobber `place_private_new` (below). No call site carries its own temp + rename code.
 Rationale: atomic-write-file 0.3.1 was the first choice, but its licence is BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`'s allow list (operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan); tempfile was already locked, MIT OR Apache-2.0.

- Its body, the private `place_private_new_with(path, bytes, mode, placed)`, runs its `placed` hook right after a `Written` placement: a forced-window test parameter, not a seam (no env read, no feature). `place_private_new_placed_copy_execs_at_once` execs the placed copy from it on Unix.

- **[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.** `hook` blocks on the channel for a dialog answer. `wait` blocks until the next driver-relevant event (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` or `dialog-expired`) and returns that event, so nothing polls and a driver parked in `wait` learns that a dialog is pending. If a dialog is already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, it returns that dialog at once (as landed by 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: `hook.dialog` is served, the dialog line is appended and signalled through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` and cleared through `WaitFeed::dialog_settled`). With an `after` past that line the driver has already seen the dialog, so `wait` blocks for the next driver-relevant event, and a driver that leaves a dialog to the human never spins. Each dialog event carries a wrapper-assigned `dialog_id` (an integer, monotonic per instance, with the counter restored from `events.ndjson` on start so an id never repeats across wrapper restarts), and `answer` names its target by that id. At most one dialog is pending per instance. A `hook.dialog` that arrives while another is pending is answered `null` at once, so that dialog renders for the human. Its event is still logged with its own `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. Whether Claude Code can hold two dialog hooks open at once (for example on parallel tool calls) is a capability-ledger row. `wait` takes an optional `after` cursor and an optional `timeout_ms`. `after` is a byte offset into the instance's `events.ndjson`.
 `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it, at once if that event is already logged, so a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`, the offset to pass as the next `after`. Without `after`, `wait` returns the next such event appended after the call. With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until an event arrives, and if the endpoint vanishes first the caller gets `instance-unreachable`, its `detail` `endpoint-lost`. On timeout it returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}`. `last` returns the `last_assistant_message` of the newest `turn-ended` event. The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start. Endpoint names are a short hash of the instance, never the raw `VIOLA_NAME` + path. Rationale: one API over Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. Accepted risk: interprocess has one main maintainer, which the seam contains.

- `viola_channel::Client::server_pid` and `tokio_client::TokioClient::server_pid` return the connected stream's peer pid through interprocess's `peer_creds().pid()` (`SO_PEERCRED`); they write and log nothing. Every frame-writing client compares that pid and the process's OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame (§Standard Contracts, Channel methods), so a squatted or rogue server is never sent a frame.

- `viola_channel` exports `peer_euid_admitted` and `peer_admitted`: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own)` is `observed == Some(own)`, so a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused. `Client::server_euid` and `TokioClient::server_euid` supply the observed euid, writing and logging nothing.
- `viola_state::liveness::server_verdict` and `verify_server` always compare the connected peer's pid and OS start time with the snapshot's: no verdict reads `Matches` without that comparison.

- `viola_state::strict::check_socket_dir` takes one `symlink_metadata`: an absent path passes, an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`, then `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as the fixed-message `Refused::NotADirectory` and anything else by the read rule; it never chmods, a refused directory stays as found. `check_endpoint_dir` is that check on a recorded endpoint's parent.
- A hold near the 3600 s ceiling is first read live at "Version done-check"; the ceiling is PROVISIONAL.

- **[Human Takeover / Wheel] Byte-source claim + atomic send window + after-the-fact confirmation, explicit release.** Any human editing key since the last turn boundary moves the wheel to the human, and `send` is refused with `human-typing`. Only a closed non-editing list never counts (the founder's live ruling F-W2, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer): focus reports (`CSI I` / `CSI O`), mouse reports (X10 `CSI M` + 3 bytes, SGR `CSI < n;n;n M|m`, urxvt `CSI n;n;n M`) and terminal replies (DA1 `CSI ? … c`, DA2 `CSI > … c`, CPR `CSI n;n R`, DECRPM `CSI ? n;n $ y`, kitty flags `CSI ? n u`, OSC replies ending BEL or ST, DCS replies ending ST, and seven further reply shapes, each after `CSI` by exact grammar, the fields compared as bytes, no intermediate byte and the field count exact: DSR status `CSI 0 n`, colour scheme `CSI ? 997;1 n` and `CSI ? 997;2 n`, window size `CSI 4;n;n t`, cell size `CSI 6;n;n t`, text area `CSI 8;n;n t`, in-band resize `CSI 48;n;n;n;n t`, modifyOtherKeys reply `CSI > 4;n m`); a host resize is no stdin byte at all. The seven joined the list at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive, ratified by the founder himself on 2026-10-08 after the exact grammars and a narrower option of two were shown (relayed verbatim by the overseer). As measured on foot 1.28.0 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/terminal-replies.md`, `evidence/reply-probe.ndjson`, `evidence/reply-probe-fixed.ndjson`): before, those seven replies of the terminal were read as typing, and a live `claude` 2.1.287 took the wheel from the driver 237 ms after it started with no key typed; after, none of 23 probe queries is read as typing, and the nearest human keys (`n`, `t`, `m`, their Alt forms, their kitty key events) and a sequence one field or one prefix away from a listed shape still take the wheel.
 A reply no terminal has been measured to write is not added on a guess. Every other byte takes the wheel: ground bytes, every other completed sequence, a sequence past 64 bytes of parameters or payload, and a C0 inside a sequence (which aborts it). A read ending on a lone ESC is the Esc key at once, and a sequence past `ESC [` / `ESC ]` / `ESC P` / `CSI M` carries across reads. The classifier only observes: the stdin observer (`run::wheel::Observed`, wrapping the host stdin handed to `viola_pty::pump_with_paste`) returns every byte whole and unchanged, and a read holding an editing key moves the wheel before it returns.
 A bridge send is written as one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR write. Human bytes arriving during that write are held in the pump and passed on straight after. An unsent `prompt-submitted` confirms and logs the take: one the hook filed `origin:"human"` moves the wheel before its line is appended (a `harness` prompt and the relabelled in-flight `driver` prompt never move it). An in-flight send whose text ends in CR or LF characters is typed without them, and one whose text holds a CR or a CR LF inside is typed with each as one LF, so its own prompt matches, is relabelled `driver` and moves no wheel (as landed at chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed for LF, at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup for CR and CRLF at the end, and at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text for a CR or a CR LF inside; [Delivery Confirmation]). A prompt that is not the in-flight send's typed text claims nothing and is appended as the hook filed it, so one filed `human` still moves the wheel.
 Harness-injected prompts are classified as harness turns, never as a human take: a prompt whose raw start (no trim) is one of `viola-agent-claude`'s four compiled `HARNESS_PREFIXES` — `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message` or `<cross-session-message` (another Claude session's message; the unescaped form is the one measured from the CLI on 2.1.287, the escaped form is relayed and kept compiled, see Tag escaping). The side effect was accepted with the widening (the founder, live, 2026-09-29 15:21:44): a human who types the cross-session tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness`. As measured on 2.1.287, and not a new ratification, a human who types `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too. The wheel starts with `driver` when `viola run` starts, so automation is accepted until the first human editing key. A `send` while a turn is running (after `prompt-submitted`, before `turn-ended`) is not queued. It is refused `not-delivered` with detail `turn-running`, and the driver calls `wait` first. A `send` that arrives while another `send` is in flight (accepted, its outcome not yet recorded) is refused the same way, never queued, and nothing is typed for it. A `prompt-submitted` of any origin marks a turn running, and `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it. A turn can end with no `turn-ended`: Claude Code's Stop hook does not fire on a user interrupt, and which hook, if any, fires for a turn that ends on an API error is a ledger row (if one does, `viola-agent-claude` registers it and maps it to `turn-ended` with a `null` `last_assistant_message`). A human interrupt is human input, so it moves the wheel to the human, and the `viola release` that returns the wheel clears the running-turn state.
 As built (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal), the running-turn state lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside the holder and cause, and records no event, snapshot field, span or obs line, so a restarted wrapper starts with no turn. The wrapper's one hook entry (`run::send::append_hook_event`) marks it before the hook's line is appended, keyed on the line's kind alone: a `prompt-submitted` of any origin (the claimed driver prompt included) marks it running, `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it, and `activity` leaves it. So a driver that read `turn-ended` through `wait` is never refused by that turn. The turn is marked ahead of a human prompt's wheel move, so a `release` landing between the two still clears it. `send` reads the wheel and then the running turn twice, in that order both times: at the send's arrival, and again once the readiness gate's wait (up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, 8.5 s) has returned ready. A human key or a turn that started during the wait is refused `human-typing` or `not-delivered` / `turn-running`, with no `send-issued` and nothing typed (the overseer's technical answer of 2026-10-07T12:10Z at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, listed for the founder as a fact; it retires the residual recorded on 2026-10-04, under which a turn starting during the wait was not refused). The wait is not interrupted when the wheel moves: `Gate` knows nothing of the wheel, so the driver hears the refusal when the wait ends. Only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears the turn, in the same lock hold as the move. A `release` on a wheel the driver already holds, `release --budget` and a refused `release` (`release-from-driver`, invalid params) leave it, as do `pause` and human keys, so a turn left running under a driver-held wheel is recovered without a keystroke by `viola pause` then `viola release`.
 An unsent human prompt moves the wheel before its line is appended, so the `send` after it reads `human-typing`, never `turn-running`, and the `release` that returns the wheel also clears that turn. `release` never empties the in-flight `send` slot, which belongs to a live send. A SessionEnd the hook appends directly (the channel did not take it) leaves the turn marked — a recorded residual; its child is ending, so no driver `send` depends on it. A driver parked in `wait` across such a turn recovers through `timeout_ms`. CLI `viola pause` moves the wheel to the human without a keystroke, after which automated `send` is refused `human-typing` with detail `manual-pause`. The wheel returns only through CLI `viola release`; a `release` on a wheel the driver already holds changes nothing and appends nothing. The wheel lives in `src/run/wheel.rs` (`WheelSlot`: holder, cause and the running turn under one lock). The in-memory move is synchronous; each change's `wheel` event (`{holder, cause}`, `source:"wrapper"`, log-only, never through the wait feed), its snapshot update, its `run.wheel_transition` span and the pending-dialog hand-back run on the wheel's own worker thread, and `viola run` flushes that worker (bounded 2 s) at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode. Every snapshot write goes through the one in-process holder `src/run/snapshot.rs` (`Snapshots`). While the wheel is `human`, the wrapper answers `hook.dialog` with `null` at once, so the dialog renders for the human without waiting out the dialog hold, and `answer` is refused `human-typing`. If the wheel moves to the human while a `hook.dialog` is already pending (a human editing key or `viola pause`), the wrapper answers that pending request with `null` at once and clears its `dialog_id`, so a dialog held by the hook is never hidden from the human for the rest of the hold.
 `budget-paused` gates only `send`, never `hook.dialog` or `answer`, because a running turn finishes. Rationale: `viola run` owns the real stdin, so it knows byte provenance exactly. The prototype paused twice on harness turns before the classifier was fixed.

- **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused with `budget-paused` through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human keys are never blocked, and a running turn finishes. The pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`. `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is, and a plain `release` returns the wheel to `driver` without lifting a budget pause. `release --budget` is sent to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only, until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under `budget.json.lock`, at three points: at start, when a `send` arrives, and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of these points, and only then is `budget-gate` appended. So a snapshot can still read `budget_paused: true` after the reset, until a `send` arrives or a turn ends, and every surface that shows the snapshot inherits that. The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, including any override, to the instance snapshot, where `list` reads it. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `src/run/budget.rs`, one `BudgetGate` per wrapper, no thread and no timer): a window is crossed only when its `used_percentage` is known and at or above its threshold and its `resets_at` is known, parses as RFC 3339 and is later than now, so a window whose `resets_at` is `"unknown"`, unparseable or passed never pauses. With both windows crossed the refusal names `five-hour`.
 The `send` point sits after the text refusals and the first `human-typing` read and before the running-turn read, so the order is `control-character` → `empty-text` → `human-typing` → `budget-paused` → `turn-running` → the readiness gate's wait; the gate is read once per `send`, never again after that wait. `answer`, `wait`, `last`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` do not read the gate (read in the diff: its five product call sites; since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the root case `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`, `tests/cli_budget.rs`, drives `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under one closed gate, each giving the exit code and the document it gives under an open one; no case drives `hook.dialog` under a closed gate). An override covers both windows until its end and is dropped at the next point after that end. It does not outlive its wrapper: every start, a revived one included, evaluates from `budget.json` alone and restores none. `release --budget` with no pause standing records nothing. `budget-gate` is appended, and the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are rewritten, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, both before the evaluation returns; a record that cannot land is an error and the recorded state stays as it was. The thresholds are read once, at the wrapper's start, and no value of either switches the gate off. The gate is fail-open: no reading, an `"unknown"` figure, a passed or unparseable `resets_at`, an unreadable or refused `budget.json` and a bad threshold each leave it open or at its default. The decision takes the wall-clock instant as an argument (no clock seam). With figures missing, viola uses the newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age. With no reading at all it records `unknown` and does not block.
 The statusline is wrapped only for sessions started by `viola run`, through a per-session settings override that then runs the user's own statusline command unchanged. A reading is recorded only when the payload holds `rate_limits`. Rationale: the per-model weekly window is hidden (claude-code#91920), so thresholds are set low. The user's global statusline config is never touched, and a visible, conservative governor supports the "ordinary individual usage" posture.

A bare pid is unsafe because pids get reused, which is why start time is matched too: a snapshot whose pid is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the heartbeat says (Session liveness). `claude agents --json` adds idle/busy status and shows unwrapped sessions as read-only rows. A `viola run` whose `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` refuses to start (exit 1, with a message naming the instance); once the endpoint exists, a name with an answering endpoint refuses the same way. `viola revive` refuses a `live` or `stale` name through the same collision check and its two stderr pairs, as the first of its four preflight readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory; a later reading is not taken once an earlier one refuses). `session-live` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips the reading, and a failed read passes (fail open). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (that chunk's `evidence/live-p4.md`), a second interactive `claude --resume <id>` of an id a live `claude` holds is neither refused nor copied: both sessions run under the one id, two writers on one transcript, so the reading stays a refusal; and after `/clear` the agents row of the session's pid names the new id (P12 follows), so a session-id join survives a `/clear` because the wrapper rewrites the snapshot's `agent_session_id` on each `session-start`. The strict-modes check on the home and the instance's files runs ahead of them, before the wrapper log opens (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor).
 A revive that passes goes through the same start as `run`, so the collision check runs twice. It resumes the `gone` instance in place: its `events.ndjson` is appended to with the earlier bytes unchanged, no launch is replayed, and its first record is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`, as every start's (the founder's answer, live, 2026-10-10, relayed by the operator: a revived start keeps the wheel at `driver`). Otherwise `run` starts in this order: program resolution (a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`; it writes nothing), collision check, pinned copy and plugin folder, version gate, exclusive bind of the endpoint (`socket_dir_ready` first, a refused or uncreatable directory the exit-1 refusal `socket-dir-refused` before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a bind that finds the name taken is an exit-1 refusal, `squatted-name`, so two concurrent starts cannot both win), first snapshot (with `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, and `statusline_command` when the named source gave a command; `pid`, `started_at`) and heartbeat, the start `wheel` and `budget-gate` events, then the child spawn, after which the snapshot is rewritten with `child_pid`. Between the first snapshot and the spawn `run` also rewrites the per-session settings override (§Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names).
 As landed by 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify every step has its place: program resolution → collision → pinned copy and plugin → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: the bounded `--version` read logged as a `version-probe` `process-start`/`process-exit` pair, the stamps read, `cli_version`/`cli_verified` carried into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; `run` prints nothing on any gate outcome) → endpoint bind (`socket_dir_ready` first, a refusal `socket-dir-refused`, exit 1, with no bind) → the budget gate at start (span `run.budget_eval` with `trigger: start`; it reads `budget.json`, restores no override and writes nothing; the thresholds were read from `config.json` earlier in the start, each rejection logged then) → first snapshot (its `budget_paused` is that verdict, its `budget_override_until` always absent) → heartbeat → start events (record two, `budget-gate`, carries that verdict's `data`, where it carried the constant `{"paused": false}` before chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) → spawn, so the child's first SessionStart hook finds a listening endpoint and a recorded snapshot. Since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the start also restores the wrapper's link set before the endpoint serves: it reads `events.ndjson` twice there (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`), the first snapshot's `links` is the restored set, the start appends no line for links and its start records are unchanged. `viola revive` starts through the same function, so a revived start's first snapshot carries the logged links.
 A gone instance's directory is reused at once, and its `events.ndjson` is appended to, never truncated.

- The snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` are also the server identity: `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` returns them with the endpoint from one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (`LiveEndpoint`, only on a real snapshot: a replayed or absent one gives none), and every frame-writing client runs the strict-modes instance check first (the CLI's `client::refuse_untrusted`, [Links]; `viola mcp`'s frame tools, [MCP]; the hook's, [Hook Contract]), then the liveness-only pre-check, then `check_endpoint_dir` on the recorded endpoint, then connects and reads `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())`, then compares the connected peer's pid and its OS start time with them before its first frame (`verify_server`; §Standard Contracts, Session liveness); the seams are `src/cmd/client.rs` `connect` with its 8 callers, `src/cmd/hook.rs` `connect` and `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` `frame`.

- **[Error Handling] thiserror 2.0.20, one enum per workspace crate (one ratified exception: `viola-pty`'s `PtyError` has a hand-written `Display`/`Error` with fixed messages, because the seam's normal dependencies are exactly portable-pty, tracing and libc; portable-pty's anyhow error is kept only as a boxed source. `viola-agent-claude`'s `AgentError` sits at the crate root and holds the stamps envelope's `StampsMalformed` beside the hook payload's `Malformed` — the second enum `StampError` was folded into it by chunk 2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness). A first open divergence, not an exception: `viola-mcp` holds `ServeError` (`Runtime`, `Initialize`, `Session`; fixed messages, returned by `serve`) beside `McpError` (`Internal`, Display `internal error`) (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); the rule stands, and its fold or ratification is open. A second: `viola-state` holds `StampsError` (`StrictModes`, `State`; fixed messages, returned by `update_stamps`) beside `StateError`, the same. Three more the census below adds, the same: `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused`. The owner of all five: a CARRY on the working-route entry "Version done-check"; anyhow 1.0.104 only in the `viola` bin: its `main`, dispatch (`cmd::dispatch` returns the error with the resolved home and instance) and the catch-site reporter `viola::obs::report_internal_error`.** `RefusalReason` lives in `viola-core`. Rationale: callers branch on refusal variants across three surfaces (channel, CLI exit codes, MCP `isError`). anyhow's context chains are only useful where a person reads them: the owner's post-mortem, which gets the chain as `chain` in `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<role>.ndjson`, never a role line, stdout or stderr.

- `AgentError` holds `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message: `resolve_program` (a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`, in the crate and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`.

- **[Deployment / Distribution] `cargo install --path .`, with the plugin compiled into the binary (KEYSTONE).** `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` are embedded via `include_str!`, and `plugin.json`'s version comes from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. At start, `viola run` copies its own exe to `<viola home>/bin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/viola` if that copy is absent, and re-hashes an existing copy before reusing it: a copy that no longer matches refuses the start (exit 1, `pinned-hash-mismatch`) and is left as found.
 It rewrites the plugin files on every start to `<viola home>/plugin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/` and substitutes the copy's path (forward slashes) into every exec-form `command` in `hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`. It then passes that folder with `--plugin-dir`, sets `VIOLA_BIN` to the copy and puts the copy's folder first on the child's PATH. `hooks.json` registers seven exec-form entries, each `"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@"` (substituted at start) with `"args": ["hook", "<kebab event>"]`: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop with `"timeout": 5`; SessionEnd with no `timeout` key; Notification, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure with `"async": true`. The dialog tier joins them (chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id): PreToolUse with `"matcher": "AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode"` and PermissionRequest, each with `"timeout": 3615` — nine exec-form entries in all. `.mcp.json` registers the server `viola` as `{"mcpServers": {"viola": {"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@", "args": ["mcp"]}}}`, the pinned copy's absolute path substituted at every start (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers; until the `mcp` verb existed it shipped `{"mcpServers": {}}`, on the operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan that a registered command that exits 2 would block Claude Code). A registered `viola mcp` that exits 1 (its home refused by `home_passes`) does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs that server's connection as failed (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings/evidence/live-round.md`). Hooks and MCP never search PATH. Rationale: the binary and the plugin can no longer drift apart. The prototype proved that PATH-found hooks run a different binary from the wrapper after a rebuild.
 The content hash is part of the key because `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` stays `0.1.0` across development rebuilds, so the version alone would collide. A rebuild therefore never changes what a running session calls. Known trade-off: a hook fix applies only to sessions started after the rebuild. The per-frame `v` + sender version stays as the second safety net, for the optional user-level install (`viola plugin install`), which is not bound to a wrapper's pinned copy.

- **[Plugin Scope] The plugin loads only into wrapped sessions via `--plugin-dir`.** Both driver and driven run under `viola run`. `viola plugin install` (a local marketplace) is optional, for the MCP verbs in an unwrapped driver. The installed plugin carries only `.mcp.json` and no hooks, so a wrapped session that also has it installed never runs two hook processes for one event (two `hook.dialog` requests for one dialog). Its `command` is the absolute path of the exe that ran `plugin install`, never a PATH lookup: as built, `viola plugin install` writes only `<home>/marketplace/` and spawns no `claude`, and its `.mcp.json` registers `viola` as `{"command": <the canonical current_exe, forward slashes>, "args": ["--home", <the canonical home, forward slashes>, "mcp"]}`, each document built by `serde_json` (`viola_agent_claude::marketplace::marketplace_files`). A wrapped session that also has the installed plugin enabled starts one `viola` MCP server, the `--plugin-dir` plugin's, and that server answers its tools: the installed plugin's `viola mcp` never starts there, and the session runs one SessionStart hook process (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings/evidence/live-round.md`: the wrapped home's `mcp.ndjson` one `process-start{subject:"self"}` and the `list` call's `agents-probe` pair, the installed home none, the CLI's MCP log one server). It is no capability-ledger row (no `send` relies on it, the ruled limit). Rationale: unwrapped sessions carry no viola hooks at all, so there is no per-tool-call spawn cost outside viola. The exceptions are `viola verify`'s transient unwrapped children, all gone when verify ends.
 The first is the print-mode probe, an unwrapped `claude -p` that loads only the `viola-verify-probe` plugin (four exec-form `hook <event> --capture` hooks) from `ledger/probes/<pid>/plugin/`. The other five are the interactive runs: Run A, untrusted in an OS-temp `viola-verify-*` dir and killed at its screen; Run B, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`; Runs C and D, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/` and `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/`, each loading the dialog-kind `viola-verify-probe` plugin; and Run E, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/`, loading the capture plugin from `ledger/probes/<pid>/resume/plugin/` and resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>`, no key typed. Runs B, C and D, as real interactive turns, also run the user's own global hooks, and Runs C and D the user's own status line (Run B's status line is the probe capture its one probe `--settings` names, [CLI Version Compatibility]), and each leaves the CLI's session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/` (an accepted residual, security-plan Data Protection): Run B three per real-CLI verify, its session, the `<id>-backup-<n>.jsonl` the CLI writes at its pasted `/compact`'s compaction and the session its pasted `/clear` opens (the last inferred, not read), and C and D one each; Run E adds none (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, `evidence/live-round.md`: the `viola-verify` transcript count 60 → 65). The print-mode probe leaves the CLI's empty project dir for its cwd `ledger/probes/<pid>/` under `~/.claude/projects/` (a `memory/` dir, no transcript), the same accepted residual (as measured on 2.1.296 and 2.1.302 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/evidence/switch-round.md`).

- **[CLI Conventions] Human text by default, `--json` for agents, a typed exit code per refusal. Prompt text comes from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument.** viola warns when an argument carries a Git Bash rewritten-path prefix. Rationale: Git Bash rewrites `/skill` arguments into Windows paths (brief §6), and agents need machine-parseable refusals. `viola revive` takes `--json` on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): every refusal of its start, a refused strict-modes check and a preflight refusal among them, prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start being `internal-error`) in place of its `unable:` / `hint:` pair where it has one, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order; without `--json` the pairs and the `--list` rows are byte-identical. A `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal.

- **[Scale / Product] Linux only.** The core runs on any current Linux distribution, CI on `ubuntu-latest`; the window features of 0.2.0 target Hyprland. No Windows or macOS code, test, fixture or CI job stands in the tree; that code is recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final` (`ecbe7ab3`).

**Ledger stamps envelope** (`ledger/stamps.json`, atomically replaced JSON, written only by `viola verify` through `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps`)
```json
{"v":1,"written_at":"2026-09-28T15:14:02.311Z","writer":"verify","data":{"versions":{"2.1.283":{"verified_at":"2026-09-28T15:14:02.311Z","rows":{"shim-resolution":"pass"},"measured":{"largest_hook_payload":{"SessionStart":412}}}}}}
```

**Security tier:** `Minimal (0), with targeted elevations for the local privilege boundary`
_Justification: viola is a local-only, single-user tool. It has no accounts, no public network listener, no database, no stored credentials and no regulated data (Sections 1, 3, 4, 5), which rules out Standard's user-account and HTTPS concerns and Hardened's compliance drivers. It still goes beyond a plain Minimal profile in two ways. First, the local IPC endpoint is effectively a code-execution interface (`send` types prompts, `answer` can allow PermissionRequest tool calls). It currently has no decided enforcement of its same-OS-user boundary, and its socket name is predictable, the socket standing in a per-user 0700 directory. Second, several state files decide what code runs and whether dialogs are answered: `snapshot.json`'s `statusline_command`, the `hooks.json` exec paths, the pinned binaries and the ledger stamps. The baseline is therefore Minimal (dependency audit, input validation on config and external payloads, error sanitization). On top of it sit specific local-boundary items: IPC endpoint access control and server impersonation, bracketed-paste breakout in `send.text`, and integrity of `~/.viola/`. Each of these traces to Section 2._

- **Networking:** local only.
  - Per-instance Unix domain sockets in a verified per-user 0700 directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`), never the `/tmp` root; no Linux abstract namespace.
  - MCP over stdio.
  - No outbound network calls by viola itself. The `claude` child handles the network to Anthropic on its own.
  - Sources: Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints); Stack (AI/ML N/A).
- **TLS:** N/A. The IPC channel is local Unix sockets, and MCP is stdio. Confidentiality in transit depends on the socket-directory and peer checks (Authentication & Authorization).

- NEVER let `config.json`, a `VIOLA_*` environment variable or a CLI flag switch off any control in this plan (the socket-directory check, the peer or server verification, the home strict-modes check, `validate_paste_text`): environment variables are not a configuration channel. The carve-outs, the two test-only seams and the terminal colour facts, switch off nothing; NEVER add another such seam or environment read without its own Decisions Log entry.

**Vector:** Filesystem state under `~/.viola/`, read across processes and holding the code-bearing artefacts Claude Code runs: its trust boundary is OS permissions on the user's home directory; readers tolerate torn lines, the pinned binary and plugin folders are never deleted in v1, and beyond the content hash in the folder name the start holds the home tree, the pinned binary and the plugin folders to the strict-modes check (owner and mode) before any log opens.

`~/.viola/` access control — the home is owner-only (0700 directories and 0600 files, the pinned `viola` 0700), every replaced file written through `replace_private`, its mode set before any byte, never relying on the umask; a strict-modes check refuses a trusted path another user can write, a home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read (any group or other bit) or a symlinked `diagnostics/` folder or file, in every process that reads a trusted file, before its first read or open under the home.

**Files (`~/.viola/`):** plaintext by design, protected by OS permissions only (0700 directories and 0600 files, the pinned `viola` 0700); the plugin files and the settings override are rewritten at every start, the override written only for a pinned path of plain characters, since a shell runs it unquoted; the pinned binary is re-hashed before use.

- NEVER create `~/.viola/`, `--home` or any file under it with the default umask. Directories are 0700 and files 0600 (`OpenOptionsExt::mode`); the only exception is the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` at 0700, and NEVER make it group- or world-writable.

- NEVER reuse an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` without re-hashing it (SHA-256, truncated) against `<hash>`, NEVER derive `<hash>` from a non-cryptographic hash (FNV, `DefaultHasher`), and NEVER reuse existing `plugin/` files without rewriting them.

The log has a start `wheel` and a `budget-gate` event, followed by `session-start` once "Verify-stamped test homes and harness" (the `boot` step-4 owner) joins it to harness readiness.

  - `run`:
    - Invokes, in order:
      1. the workspace unit and integration tests (`cargo test`)
      2. fake-agent E2E against `fixtures/claude/*`
      3. none in 0.1.0: the browser suite left with the browser leg, and the mutation step keeps its number 4
      4. mutation testing scoped to the chunk diff (Founder Direction 1: "surviving mutants are red") — only under `run --mutants`, never in the default or `--all`; its cadence is the epoch-boundary code audit
    - Exit 0 only if every suite passes and no mutant survives. Non-zero otherwise, with a JSON summary on stdout (suite, passed, failed, survived).
    - Local-only mode adds `viola verify` against the real CLI. It must never run in CI (arch excerpt, CI/CD).
  - `status`:
    - Queries `viola list --json --home <tmp>`.
    - The agent polls per item: `name`, `wrapped`, `liveness`, `status`, `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `dialog_pending`, `cli_verified`.
    - It also polls the envelope `skipped{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and `budget`.
  - `cleanup`:
    - Stops every wrapper started by `boot`. Exit is confirmed on the process handle, not EOF.
    - Deletes the temp home and verifies the endpoint is gone: a CLI verb against the name returns exit 21, and a connect to the socket path is refused or the path is absent; `cleanup` removes no leftover socket file, so a force-killed wrapper's file stays until a next bind of that name takes it over.
    - Must be idempotent: a second run exits 0 and reports nothing to clean.
  - `logs`:
    - Prints, as JSON lines, the structured per-process logs of `run` / `hook` / `mcp` / `cli` in the §3 log format (Founder Direction 3; the exact field set is not in the distilled excerpt, so Phase 3 pins it).
    - Also prints `instances/<name>/events.ndjson` and the hook trace under `diagnostics/`.
    - Filterable by instance and kind.
    - Retention is the lifetime of the temp home: events are never truncated (arch excerpt, Event line), and `cleanup` deletes the home.

- A refusal prints `unable` plus `reason  detail`, then one `hint:` line, keyed by the reason (or by reason · detail where listed):
  - `human-typing`: `the human has the wheel; send again after the human hands it back`
  - `budget-paused`: `budget gate is closed; it lifts at the window reset, or when the human lifts it`
  - These two refusals reach drivers, and a driver's `release` is refused (`-32602`, `release-from-driver`, exit 20). So no hint ever names `viola release` (T3). `release` stays a human verb, documented under Wheel, link and gate verbs.
  - `unverified-cli`: `run viola verify for this CLI version`
  - `not-delivered · turn-running`: `a turn is running; viola wait <name> first`
  - `not-delivered · control-character`: `the text contains a control character (only LF, CR, TAB are allowed)`
  - `not-delivered · empty-text`: `the text is empty once its trailing newlines are removed; send a text with content`
  - `not-delivered · input-not-ready`: `<name> was not ready for input; send again, and if it repeats a human must look at the session`
  - `not-delivered · no-prompt-submitted`: `<name> did not submit the prompt; check it, then send again` (the sample above)
  - `not-delivered · unknown-dialog`: `that dialog is not pending; viola list shows the current DIALOG`
  - `instance-unreachable` (exit 21) has one hint per cause, because the code is shared (T4):
    - no wrapper is running for the name: `<name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances`
    - the name is an unwrapped session: `<name> is not a wrapped session; only sessions started with viola run take commands`
    - a wrapper lost with the call open (`endpoint-lost`): `<name>'s wrapper went away during the call; viola list shows whether it is still running` (last on stderr, plain ASCII).
    - the home or the instance's state files fail the strict-modes check (`send` after reading its text; `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` first; each before any frame): no `unable  instance-unreachable` line and no hint of this list, but the fixed instance-state pair `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only` (pattern 1, Refusal), not the `[/ ]` mirror; under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`
    - server verification fails: `the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted`
    - the socket directory is refused: the hint of `run`'s socket-directory pair below
  - The exit-1 start refusals of `viola run` have one fixed-message line and one hint per cause (T4). None of them shows a path or a pid:
    - `unable: <name> is already live` → `hint: viola list`
    - `unable: <name> is still running but not answering` (stale heartbeat, live pid) → `hint: viola list shows it as stale; stop that process before starting <name> again`
    - These two print and log their own codes: a stale holder `stale-heartbeat`; a live holder and a fresh replayed beat `already-live`.
    - `unable: the endpoint for <name> is held by another process` (squatted name) → `hint: another process holds this name's endpoint; stop it or pick another name`
    - `unable: the pinned viola copy failed its integrity check` (SHA-256 mismatch) → `hint: the pinned copy was changed after it was written, so viola will not run it`
    - `unable: <name>'s command is a .cmd or .bat script` (Windows) → `hint: pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim`
    - `unable: the viola home is not private to you` (a home-level refusal of the home-tree check made at start before any log, of the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, the pinned copy and its `plugin/<key>/`, each that exists; no child) → `hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions`; an instance-level refusal of the same check prints `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` → `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`
    - `unable: the socket directory for <name> cannot be trusted` (before any snapshot, child or bind) → `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions`
  - The exit-1 refusals of `viola revive` take the same form, one fixed-message line and one hint per cause, read in a fixed order that stops at the first refusal. None of them shows the recorded directory, a pid or a logged id, and no hint names `viola release`:
    - `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` (strict-modes on the instance's files) → `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`
    - `unable: <name> is already live` and its stale sibling: `run`'s two lines and hints above, unchanged
    - `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume` → `hint: start one: viola run <name> -- claude`
    - `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` (an `--id` the log does not hold) → `hint: viola revive <name> --list`
