- Lint: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings`.
  - `[workspace.lints.clippy]` denies `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` and `dbg_macro`, and every product member inherits it (`[lints] workspace = true`, asserted by `tests/contract_lints.rs`). `viola-e2e` opts out and denies only `dbg_macro`, because the harness prints its JSON document. The fake agent carries a crate-level print allow. The root bin carries no print allow: its only human writer is the `human` module, `src/human.rs` (which holds `write_refusal`, `write_internal_error`, `write_result` and their wrappers) and its phases under `src/human/`. On stderr, `write_refusal` writes the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` lines as ONE `write_all` and `write_internal_error` writes exactly `error: internal error\n`; on stdout, `write_result` writes one line per `write_all`. The `refuse` / `internal_error` / `result` wrappers lock the stream, call the writer and drop the result (a closed pipe is swallowed, never a panic), a form `print_stdout`/`print_stderr` do not flag. Its callers are the `viola run` start refusals (live or stale name, tampered pinned copy, squatted endpoint, a refused home tree), `viola verify` (its refusals, step lines and `stamped` summary), the CLI frame verbs' instance-state refusal (`client::refuse_untrusted`, shared with `viola link` / `viola unlink`), `viola send` (its readback mirror), `viola wait` / `viola last` (their result and context lines through the message-mode escaper `escape_message`, and the `unable` + `hint:` pair as ONE write, `write_unable`), `viola answer` (`write_answered`, `answer_hint`) and the `main` catch site, which prints `error: internal error` for every `cli` verb without `--json`, and under `--json` the `internal-error` document on stdout in its place (`cmd::internal_error_document`), stderr empty; `hook` and obs never call it.
  - `clippy.toml` `disallowed-macros` bans `tracing::{info,warn,error,debug,trace}`, so `obs_event!` is the only sanctioned emitter. Raw `event!` is caught by a fail-closed grep in `scripts/lint-probes.sh`, because clippy 1.98.1 cannot exempt a macro's inner expansion (obs-plan §3 logger-stack-install).
  - `scripts/lint-probes.sh` proves every ban fires and every control passes, as `deny-probes.sh` does for cargo-deny.

- Dependency policy: `cargo deny check` over `deny.toml` — advisories, licences (`allow` exactly `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `Zlib`, `Unicode-3.0`; `0BSD` only through the per-crate `[[licenses.exceptions]]` for `doctest-file`, the one 0BSD crate interprocess 2.4.4 pulls into the Linux graph, never through `allow`: operator ratification 2026-09-25, security-plan Decisions Log), sources (crates.io only) and bans: C-building crates (`cc`, `libsqlite3-sys`, `openssl-sys`), telemetry crates (`opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`, `sentry`, `tracing-appender`) and feature bans (`veil/toggle`, `rmcp` `auth` / `transport-streamable-http-server`, `tracing-subscriber/env-filter`, `serde_json/unbounded_depth`, so every parse of external bytes keeps serde_json's default recursion limit, its probe row `serde_json-unbounded-depth`), evaluated for the one target triple `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. The ban on `tokio` anywhere in the normal dependency graph, direct or transitive, of `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-state` and `viola-agent-claude` (the four crates of `scripts/sync-crates.txt` since chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) lives in `deny-sync.toml` (the same one triple, `exclude-dev = true`) and runs once per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, that crate as the sole root: `cargo deny --config deny-sync.toml --manifest-path crates/<crate>/Cargo.toml check bans`. Never a direct-parent allowlist (`wrappers`), because Tokio could otherwise arrive unnoticed through a third-party feature such as interprocess's or notify's; never `--exclude` over the workspace, which false-fails under feature unification — a shared crate's optional `tokio` feature stays on after the crate enabling it is excluded (as measured at chunk 2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates, research.md §Measured facts, cargo-deny 0.19.4 and 0.20.2). Limit, same measurement: the crate owning the optional `tokio` feature (`viola-channel`) false-fails as its own root once `viola-mcp` enables that feature (`cargo metadata` reports the unified set), and no listed sync crate depends on it (`[premise-corrected]` at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers: the code-graph crate-edges query found no edge from a listed crate into `viola-channel`). So `viola-channel` left `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, and its normal graph without its feature is covered by `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`: `cargo tree -p viola-channel -e normal --target all -i tokio --prefix none` must print no `tokio v` line (absence read from the printed line, never the exit: exit 0 "nothing to print" once tokio is in `Cargo.lock`, exit 101 "did not match" while it is not), and its control with `--features tokio` must print one; verdict `channel-tokio-free: ok`, run in CI's supply-chain step after the sole-root loop. Every ban is proven live by `scripts/deny-probes.sh`: a throwaway project per ban must fail with that ban's own diagnostic, and a clean control must pass both configs; its `channel-tokio-edge` probe (a throwaway workspace with a normal tokio edge must fail the tree form) and its channel control (the same edge behind a `tokio` feature must pass) prove the tree form fires (`deny-probes: 14/14 banned, control clean`, the count one per `probes=(` row of `scripts/deny-probes.sh` plus the planted `channel-tokio-edge`). `fuzz/` has its own `Cargo.lock` outside this graph, and its libfuzzer-sys builds C++ via `cc`: the only C build in the repository. The operator ratified this on 2026-09-24 as a test-only exemption. The crate is never linked into `viola`, and `fuzz` never joins the root `[workspace]`. Its lockfile is audited separately: the CI `supply-chain` step `Fuzz lockfile audit (advisories, sources)` runs `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --format json check advisories sources` into `target/supply-chain/deny-fuzz.json`, and the weekly nightly `advisories` job runs `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories`. Before the first write, `diagnostics/` and every opened diagnostics file (role file, and later the detail file) get the same checks as the home: `lstat` owner == `geteuid()`, `mode & 0o077 == 0`, not a symlink (files opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`). A failed check is handled like a failed open (below), so a pre-existing foreign, permissive or symlinked diagnostics file is never written. Open the role file with `OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true)` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode(0o600)`. If the open fails, the writer becomes `std::io::sink` (or stderr for `mcp` only, D-09). The instance detail file `<home>/instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson` is **not** opened here. It is opened lazily, with the same append / 0600 / 0700 rules, by the first content-bearing record (chain, drift report), and the panic hook opens it itself when it is still closed. A failed detail open drops only the detail line, never the home-level line, and writes nothing to stderr. The error-free `hook` path therefore keeps exactly one log `open` (D-29).

- **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.8.1` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF. The host stdin handed to the pump is `viola_pty::host_stdin()`, which is `std::io::stdin()`. Its callers are `run`'s pump and the fake agent. Rationale: 0.8.1 is spike-proven (S1, O1 render stress, the Pulse live test, and about an hour driving this arch session in Windows Terminal with no PTY defect). 0.9.0's Windows garbage-read bug (wezterm#6783) does not bear on a Linux-only build; moving `portable-pty` off `=0.8.1` is owed to the working-route entry "Version done-check" (RUSTSEC-2026-0441, below). Swap triggers: portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 if the O1 stray-spaces artifact reproduces only under `viola run` (then test `PASSTHROUGH_MODE`). `viola run` puts its own host terminal into raw mode for the run through `HostTerminal` (Unix termios) and restores the saved modes on Drop; off a terminal it is a no-op.
 The child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory. A revived start has the one other source: `viola revive` sets the child's cwd to the instance snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the directory the first start spawned its child in. It reads that value only after the strict-modes check on the instance's files, and it must name an existing directory, else the revive is refused `cwd-missing`. Program resolution and the version gate never read the recorded directory: the program is looked up on the reviving process's own `PATH`, from its own current directory (a boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-10, after it was shown to him as one, the overseer and the operator as relay; chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive). viola resolves the child program to an absolute path itself. The pump keeps the input writer until the child exits. The exit is recorded as `exit_source` `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback`.
 viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize ([Human Takeover / Wheel]). A test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first.
 `viola_pty::pty_backend()` is always `openpty`, and `viola_pty::host_size()` reads `TIOCGWINSZ`.

- `target/viola-answers-*/` (under the test process's current dir): the `tempfile` dir of `src/cmd/hook.rs`'s unit case `answer_reads_no_relative_answers_dir_that_resolves`, reached only by the relative path `../<current dir's name>/target/<tmp>/answers` and removed on drop, gitignored. It sits under the current dir, not the OS temp dir. `viola` never reads it by that name.

All are 0700 and removed when verify passes, fails, or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (a drop guard each; the repo's `.gitignore` carries `/.viola-verify-*/` for a leftover). The stop is `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` (`cmd::verify::stop`, installed by `viola verify` alone; its handler only sets one flag every wait reads). A stopped run kills and reaps its child with no key, and its guards remove only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing; it adds no owner record and no remover of an earlier run's or another process's dirs. SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install (ignored, fail-open) keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand: the founder's narrow entry (relayed by the overseer, 2026-10-10), and the event set the operator's P4 answer (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). Run C's one `allow` runs `touch viola-probe-permission` inside its own dir; Run D's plan file lands inside its own dir, never under `~/.claude/plans` (as measured on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287: `~/.claude/plans/` 17 → 17 files across the re-run). These are the founder's live rulings on the dirs (2026-10-05 08:25Z) and on M7 = A and STOP 7 (2026-10-05), relayed by the overseer.

**Section:** §Threat Model Summary (body: the tier justification, Networking; threat-model-summary.md: the IPC vector) · §Authentication & Authorization (body: Auth approach, IPC access control (Windows) retired; authentication-authorization.md: IPC access control (Unix) and its directory check, the IPC access control (Windows) row and its two witnesses retired) · §Data Protection (body: TLS) · §Security Anti-Patterns (body and security-anti-patterns.md: the no-switch-off ban; body: the listener and client-pipe bans retired) · §Bootstrap phases (body: auth-scaffolding-baseline; bootstrap-phases.md: the viola-channel line)

- The socket is chmod 0600 right after the bind, `ListenerOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` unused because chmod after the bind is the one form (was because interprocess returns `Unsupported` on macOS); `check_socket_dir` has no off-Unix `Ok(())` arm.

**Why:** the founder's own rulings of 2026-11-04 (three, the last at 2026-11-04 21:53Z; inputs#I1, inputs#I5 item 6): viola is Linux-only, the Windows and macOS code cut, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final` (`ecbe7ab3`); the chunk removed `server/win.rs`, the named-pipe arms and the macOS socket-directory arm.

## 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci — client server verification is one Linux flow; the macOS carve-out and the Windows SQOS open retired
**Section:** §Authentication & Authorization (body: the library row, IPC client-side server verification; authentication-authorization.md: the server verification, peer pid, peer euid, verdict, link / unlink and witness rows; the exiting-wrapper Windows pipe, macOS cases and macOS carve-out rows retired) · §Bootstrap phases (bootstrap-phases.md: the viola-channel client line) · §Error Handling (error-handling.md: hook, mcp) · §Input Validation (input-validation.md: the frame verbs) · §Security Anti-Patterns (body and security-anti-patterns.md: the frame-before-verification ban, the peer-euid seam ban) · §Threat Model Summary (threat-model-summary.md: the IPC vector)

**Why:** the founder's own rulings of 2026-11-04 (inputs#I1, inputs#I5 item 6), Linux-only; the chunk removed the SQOS open arms, `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` (their Linux value folded) and `server_verdict`'s `peer_pid_reported` parameter.

body:
## 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci — the three-runner greens re-worded as dated readings
**Section:** Cognitive Accessibility › Timeout extensions (cognitive-accessibility.md: the closed-gate case); keyboard-test-harness.md (Tooling: the revive, statusline and budget readings)
**Change:**
- `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone` reads green as measured at CI run 38098238731 (was green on the three CI runners).
- keyboard-test-harness's revive, statusline and budget-gate readings read green in CI (was green on the three CI runners), their chunks and runs kept.
**Why:** the CI matrix moved to `[ubuntu-latest]`, and a dated measurement on the retired legs is re-worded by its owner, never left as current.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-05T13-05-41-wrap/

- **Automated tools per surface:**
  - **web-spa:** none in 0.1.0: the frontend is deferred to 0.2.0 and its technology is not chosen
  - **Mobile:** N/A (phone view deferred)
  - **CLI / TUI:** assert_cmd + trycmd + portable-pty outer-PTY output-discipline checks on the `ubuntu-latest` CI leg, Linux only (the frame verbs' server-verify peer pid witness, the socket-directory refusal and the stale-row dim witness `cross_list_rows_dim_a_stale_row_end_to_end_on_a_terminal` among them); manual Orca passes (Linux) supplemental only
5. **screen-reader-test-spec-setup** — none in 0.1.0; the manual Orca pass stays founder-owned

6. **a11y-ci-gate-wire** — none of its own: the cli / tui cases run inside the `test` job's `coverage` suite (matrix `[ubuntu-latest]`) under `gate --require coverage,doctest` (skips never allowed), and no a11y lint, aggregation or upload step exists

- NEVER block, refuse or delay a human keystroke in `viola run`, or in a start a passed `viola revive` made, past the current atomic paste, and never count focus / mouse / resize sequences or terminal replies as editing (P4).

- The statusline-bearing start (as landed, chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through): `passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes` (`tests/tui_passthrough.rs`) is its reading of the zero-viola-bytes clause, green in CI (run 38080855246). `viola hook statusline`'s 5 s PROVISIONAL bound falls on the user's own command, never on a keystroke or the human. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.

- The budget pause (as landed, chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) is a bound on the driver only: an automated `send` is refused `budget-paused` (exit 11) until the window's reset or `viola release <name> --budget`, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed. Its reading: `path6_a_reading_over_the_threshold_refuses_the_send` (`tests/cli_budget.rs`) — a human key reaches the child under a closed gate and the outer PTY holds none of viola's literals, green in CI (run 38091081413). `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` are not gated: read in the diff, and held since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links by `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone` (each gives under a closed gate the exit code and document it gives under an open one).

- cli: no interactive prompt, pager or redraw, and input is stdin / `--file` only; tui: the terminal belongs to the child (under `viola revive --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: viola writes nothing past it, and a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel), and human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or delayed past the atomic paste, and focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) are never counted as editing; every other byte is. The page's tab order is deferred with the frontend to 0.2.0.

- The a11y harness is the tests' own assert_cmd / predicates / trycmd / portable-pty cases (cli output discipline, tui boundary), run by `scripts/agent-run.* run` inside the `test` job's `coverage` suite (matrix `[ubuntu-latest]`) under `gate --require coverage,doctest` (skips never allowed); 0.1.0 runs no browser a11y leg.

- Colour decision order (first match → no colour): `--json` · `viola run` · `viola hook`/`mcp` · `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included) · `TERM=dumb` · non-TTY stdout. SGR only for amber `DIALOG`, dim `stale` rows, bold NAME — always beside its word; never on `unable` / `fail`. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), `list` is uncoloured under any rung above; on a terminal that takes colour every NAME value is bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog takes the attention token (its kind word plain), a wrapped `stale` row is dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, the spans are laid over the escaped, padded cells (the plain board's columns, one write), and the depth is truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM` (`COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read). A wrapped row joined to one `claude agents --json` read by child pid or agent session id reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; each unjoined session follows under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME its `sessionId`, LIVE `live`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, with no separator when there is none and the board as with no `claude` on a failed read. With the terminal's width known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...`, never inside an escape; a wrapped NAME is never cut, and a piped board or `--json` keeps every name whole.

- Frames: `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` before `read_line` (over → `-32600` + close); `behavior`, `dialog_id` (u64), wheel holder and dialog kind are closed types; `link`/`unlink` names through `ViolaName::try_new`; optional additive `conn`. On Unix the wrapper's `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))`: a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file, writing no line, nothing on the terminal and moving no wheel. Before its first frame every client (CLI `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, `viola hook`'s `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, `viola mcp`'s four frame tools) compares, on Linux, the connected stream's peer pid (`Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid`, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`) and that process's OS start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` from its one snapshot read, after the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted` for the eight CLI verbs, the hook's `trusted` for `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, `strict::check_instance` in the MCP frame tools; a refusal writes no frame and no line), that read being `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` and only a real snapshot going on to the comparison (`viola_state::liveness::verify_server` → the closed `ServerVerdict` `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`; only `Matches` lets a frame be written); ahead of that comparison each client checks the recorded endpoint's directory before it connects (`viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir`; a refused directory writes no frame: CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, MCP the same with no log line, `viola hook` failing open, exit 0, empty streams, one WARN `hook-decision` of `detail` `socket-dir-refused`) and then, on Unix, the connected peer's euid (`viola_channel::peer_admitted` over `Client::server_euid` / `TokioClient::server_euid`, a foreign euid or one it cannot read reading `server-verify-failed`); a refused euid, a mismatch or a check that cannot be made writes no frame (CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable`; MCP `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no log line; `viola hook` fails open, exit 0, no body, its `hook-decision` line carrying `server-verify-failed`). No check sits inside `viola_channel::Client::connect` (`viola-channel` has no `viola-state` edge): they stand at the three seams, `cmd::client::connect`, `cmd::hook`'s `connect` and `viola-mcp`'s `frame`. Method params are each method's: `wait`'s `after` / `timeout_ms` are absent or a `u64`, and `from` (read by `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer` and `pause`) is absent, `null` or a valid `ViolaName`, anything else `-32602` with `data: null` (the envelope types none of them).

- Human text by default (`viola list`'s human mode alone reads `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM` in every build, never set, only to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written: none under `--json`, a non-terminal stdout, `NO_COLOR` present or `TERM` exactly `dumb`; they configure nothing and reach no log line, error or refusal; `COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read), `--json` for agents (`viola revive` takes it on both arms, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract: a refused strict-modes check, a preflight refusal or any refusal of the start it shares with `run` is the exit-1 `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with stderr empty, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error` through `client::refused_document`, and `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; `Launch.json` makes `refused_with` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) print the document in place of the human pair for `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name` and `socket-dir-refused`, and a program not found `internal-error`, each before `spawn_child`; an anyhow error from `trusted`, `checked_exe`, `open_wrapper_log`, `preflight` or `start` prints the `internal-error` document and returns the same error, so the catch site logs its chain and its line; a `pump_child` error prints no document, the child having held the terminal; `viola plugin install --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}` with no path, exit 0, and its refused strict-modes check the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, exit 21, through `client::unreachable_document`; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; _Known issues, non-obvious constraints, and things that have broken before. Extracted from `doc:architecture` and the specialist plans (measured facts and research findings) by `/andromeda-setup-project`._

**What breaks:** waiting for reader EOF to detect child exit breaks the rule that child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF (`pty_backend()` is `openpty`; the ConPTY that never closed its output stream left with the Windows code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`).
**How to avoid:** detect exit only by `wait()` on the process handle (a dedicated handle-wait thread); tests use `child.wait()`, never master EOF.
**Fix if broken:** move exit detection to the handle; log `process-exit{exit_source:"handle-wait"}`.
**References:** arch [PTY]; brief §4.1 Windows details; test-plan §11 E2E.

**What breaks:** 0.9.0's Windows garbage-read bug (wezterm#6783) does not bear on a Linux-only build; the pin stands on 0.8.1 being spike-proven.
**How to avoid:** keep `=0.8.1` behind the `pty` seam; moving it off `=0.8.1` (RUSTSEC-2026-0441) is owed to the working-route entry "Version done-check"; the named swap is portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 if the O1 stray-spaces artifact reproduces only under `viola run`.
**References:** arch [PTY]; security §Data Protection (handle inheritance).

**What breaks:** spawning `claude` by name on Windows hits the npm `.cmd` shim; portable-pty builds its own `CreateProcessW` line without std's BatBadBut escaping.
**How to avoid:** viola resolves the child program to an absolute path itself (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and spawns that; its one refusal is `ProgramNotFound`.
**References:** brief §4.1; security §Input Validation (child executable resolution).

**What breaks:** locking the file you append to breaks the kept layout: lock files are separate, a layout chosen while Windows (where append + exclusive lock fails, rust-lang/rust#54118) was a target, and kept.
**How to avoid:** every guarded file has its own `<name>.lock` sibling; lock that, append to the data file with one `write` per line.
**References:** arch [Database / State Store].

**What breaks:** the macOS socket-path cap left with the macOS code; on Linux the endpoint is `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`), never the `/tmp` root.
**How to avoid:** short hashed names in a per-user 0700 dir; `run` records the resolved `endpoint` in the snapshot and every other process connects to the recorded path (a child may see a different `TMPDIR`).
**References:** arch Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints); security amendment 2.

**What breaks:** started from inside a Claude session, the child inherits `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the Remote Control bridge and the messaging socket/token (11 names measured on the Windows host).
**How to avoid:** the R8 rule: `viola-agent-claude::plan_strip` removes every inherited `CLAUDE*` name matched exactly, except a name in `config.json` `claude_env_keep`, and always the 11-name `IDENTITY_FLOOR`; log names only (`env_stripped_count` / `env_stripped_known` / `env_kept`), never values.
**References:** brief §4.1 S6; arch Occupied Resources → Environment variables; security Decisions Log 2026-09-25; obs D-34.

**What breaks:** on the retired Windows runner (its code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) a key written into ConPTY right after `ResizePseudoConsole` returned was never read by the Rust test child, which was blocked in its console read (`ReadConsoleW` through Rust's stdin): measured 13 losses in 200 isolated iterations (6.5 %) of `spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code` under `cargo llvm-cov nextest` on `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260922.246.2 (ci#36527891850, job 109274838484). Every loss was class K: the child's size watcher saw the new size with no key, viola's writer had written and flushed the key, and ConPTY wrote no cursor-position request (`dsr-cpr 0`). The loss lies between the ConPTY input-pipe write and that test child's read; **where inside that span, and why, is not established** — an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source (relayed at the wrap, not verified here) found no input-buffer flush on the resize path and no reported resize input loss, so this is not recorded as a ConPTY defect. This host's conhost 10.0.26100.8875 read 20/20.
**The product window — open and unmeasured for `claude`:** viola forwards resizes and keys as they come and never holds, queues or reorders a human key behind a resize (a11y-plan §1), so nothing in viola closes this window. Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, reading with `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize in `viola run` is **unmeasured**; the rate above is the Rust test child's. Owner: the open residuals of origin `2026-11-04T23-11-43-wrap` (target `another-os`). The founder's product question on H2 stays open.
**How to avoid (tests only):** a test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first — the red test now waits for its watcher's `size 120x40` line, and read 200/200 under the same loop (ci#36529038462). That reshaped test does NOT cover the product window: it proves the key arrives once the resize has landed, not that a key racing a resize arrives, and it reads with the Rust child, never `claude`.
**Fix if broken:** read the kept reports in `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/` (`<test>.<pid>.report`, `<test>.<pid>.test.report`, `<pid>` the test process's id) by the chunk's localisation rule — class R (no `size` line), K (size seen, key flushed, key lost) or E (key before size) — before changing any wait; never raise `CHILD_WITHIN` or retry the test.
**With the sideloaded ConPTY** (removed with the Windows code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) (chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty`, one windows-2025 run, image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587, ci#36563868040, the measurement-only race): sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` 1.24.260710001 lost 0 of 200, the inbox ConPTY 14 of 200 — no rate claimed, and the product window above stays unmeasured for `claude`.
**References:** arch [PTY]; test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY, §10 Zero-flakiness budget; chunk `2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe` `evidence/h2-reproduction.md`; chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty` `evidence/h2-with-without.md`; microsoft/terminal PR #19535 (post-resize CPR — not seen on either build).

**What breaks:** on Windows x64 (code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) the sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` wrote `ESC[1t ESC[c ESC[?1004h ESC[?9001h` at spawn, and the child's start waits until the DA1 query `ESC[c` is answered. A real terminal answers at once; a `viola run` whose stdio is pipes (or any host that never answers) holds the child ~3 s (measured on the dev host: 3.54 s unanswered vs 0.54 s answered, 0.48 s on the inbox host). The answer travels through viola's pump, so the child's start now also waits for the pump.
**How to avoid:** a test that drives `viola run` on pipes answers DA1 the way a terminal would (`tests/support/piped.rs` `Piped` answers `ESC[?1;0c`); viola itself stays silent and never answers. A test timing a window around the child's start keys on the wrapper's `process-start{claude-child}` line, not the child's `start` receipt.
**Open:** the stall of a headless `viola run` is a product finding, a Windows-only finding, left with the Windows code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`.
**References:** arch [PTY]; test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY; chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty` `evidence/da1-stall.md`.

**What breaks:** on the retired Windows build (its code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) a `viola hook` fired within milliseconds of the wrapper's exit could still reach the exiting wrapper's own `\\.\pipe\viola-<h12>`: measured at ci#36532038635 (`test (windows-2025)`), where the test's hook connected and wrote its `hook.event` 25 ms after the wrapper's `process-exit` line, after the test had seen the wrapper's exit code. `viola hook` still exits 0 silently (fail-open holds), but the notification reads as delivered, so `SessionEnd`'s direct-append fallback is skipped in that window. **Why the pipe outlives the observed exit is not established** — Microsoft's documented `ExitProcess` order closes handles before the exit status is set, which argues against the obvious reading. A pipe-name collision with another home is ruled out: the endpoint name carries the home.
**How to avoid (tests):** "stopped" means the endpoint is gone — a client connect reads NotFound, on Unix refused or NotFound (the harness `endpoint_gone` rule, on Unix through `unconnectable`) — never the exit code alone: the root fixture's `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` wait for it (`wait_endpoint_gone`). After a kill the rule differs: a killed wrapper removes nothing, so on Unix its socket file stays and a wait on the file being absent never ends; `Wrapper::kill` waits on `holder_gone` (a connect to the path refused or the path absent).
**References:** test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget; obs-plan §6 fail-open `detail` codes; chunk `2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness` research.md §Item 8.

**What breaks:** on this host `CARGO_HOME` sits on another drive (the registry is not under `~/.cargo`), so a path to a crate's source built from `~/.cargo/registry/src/…` or a guessed `CARGO_HOME` reads nothing, and a search over it reads as "not found".
**How to avoid:** locate a crate's source through `cargo metadata --format-version 1`: the package's `manifest_path` is its `Cargo.toml`, and its parent is the source root at the exact version the lockfile resolved.

The wrapper channel: JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson on interprocess 2.4.4 local sockets — one endpoint per `viola run` (the Unix socket `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`, never the `/tmp` root). It provides a sync client and server; behind its `tokio` feature (`tokio = ["dep:tokio", "interprocess/tokio"]`) it holds the Tokio client `tokio_client::TokioClient` (`connect`, `conn`, `request`; landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), enabled by `viola-mcp` and, in a package-scoped test build, by the crate's own `fake-agent = ["tokio"]`; without the feature its normal graph stays tokio-free (`scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`). It owns the endpoint name (hand-written FNV-1a 64), framing with `MAX_FRAME`, the result / refusal / error shapes, the one fault reader `sanitised_fault` of `reply_of` and `of_reply` (`None` without an integer `code`; each of the five codes reads its fixed `message` and a closed `data` or null; a code outside the five reads `{"code": <code>, "message": "wrapper fault", "data": null}`), the Unix listener hardening, the peer euid decision (`peer_euid_admitted`, `peer_admitted`; a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused), the connected server's euid (`Client::server_euid` / `TokioClient::server_euid`, writing and logging nothing) and the connected server's peer pid (`Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid`) that every frame-writing client's server check (`viola_state::liveness::verify_server`) compares with the snapshot before its first frame.

`viola-core` (`RefusalReason`, `ViolaName`, `MAX_FRAME`, `v`); interprocess 2.4.4; serde, serde_json, thiserror, tracing, veil (as landed); libc (the uid for the socket dir); tokio `io-util` and `interprocess/tokio` behind the optional `tokio` feature (dev-dependency tokio `rt`).

The wrapper (`run`) server side; clients `hook`, the CLI verbs, `viola-mcp` (Tokio client) and the tests' raw-frame clients. Tests only: the `test-support` feature (`pub mod test_support`: `JsonFields`, the tracing field visitor) — enabled only by the root `[dev-dependencies]`, never in a release build (release-check refuses it).

- Listener: 0700 per-user dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` or `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`, never the `/tmp` root) checked before bind and before connect by `viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir` (one `symlink_metadata`; an absent path passes; a symlink, a non-directory, another owner or any group or other bit is refused, `socket-dir-refused`, left as found and never chmodded), never inside `viola_channel::Client::connect`: `viola-channel` has no `viola-state` edge, so the check stands at the channel seam's callers; socket chmod 0600 after the bind (never `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`); `.lock` sibling as the start arbiter; `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))` (`peer_creds` euid), so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file and writing no line; `Server::serve` injects `peer_admitted` as a `type Admission` through the private `serve_admitting`, with no env, flag or feature seam. `try_overwrite` off.

- Client: `Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid` return the connected stream's peer pid through interprocess's `peer_creds().pid()` (Linux `SO_PEERCRED`), writing and logging nothing. Before its first frame every frame-writing client (CLI `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, `viola hook`'s `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, `viola-mcp`'s four frame tools) first runs the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted` for the CLI verbs, the hook's `trusted`, `strict::check_instance` in the MCP frame tools; a refused check writes no frame and no line), then takes its one snapshot read (the CLI frame verbs and `viola-mcp`'s frame tools the liveness-only `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` read, `LiveEndpoint`: endpoint, pid, start time from one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` read, only on a real snapshot; `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths one shared `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` before `Client::connect_by`, a replayed or absent snapshot unreachable), then checks the recorded endpoint's directory (`viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir`; a refusal writes no frame: CLI exit 21 / MCP `instance-unreachable`, its `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, the hook fails open with no body), connects, reads the connected peer's euid on Unix (`peer_admitted` over `Client::server_euid` / `TokioClient::server_euid`), then compares that peer pid and its OS start time with the snapshot's `pid` / `started_at` (`viola_state::liveness::verify_server` → `ServerVerdict`); a foreign or unreadable euid, a mismatch or a check that cannot be made writes no frame (CLI exit 21 / MCP `instance-unreachable`, its `detail` `server-verify-failed`, the hook fails open with no body); a refused strict-modes check's `detail` is `strict-modes-failed`, a client with no live endpoint reads `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`, and the CLI's `answer_of` and MCP's `of_reply` read `Connect` as `instance-dead` and `Closed | Io` as `endpoint-lost`. A peer pid not reported is a check that cannot be made (`server_verdict` → `Unverifiable`), so no frame is written.
- The recorded snapshot `endpoint` is authoritative (children may see another environment).
- Linux abstract-namespace names are never used: they carry no filesystem permissions and any local user could connect.

- **IPC boundaries** (viola-channel JSON-RPC over interprocess 2.4.4 local sockets):
  - `corr` carries the JSON-RPC `id` on channel lines, `dialog_id` on dialog and hook lines, and the send `cursor` on send lines (tests).
  - **Additive `conn` field (D-10).** The client generates `conn = "<process>-<pid>-<t0>-<n>"`, with `t0` the process's start instant in Unix epoch milliseconds (captured once at init; Low sensitivity like `pid`) and `n` a per-process connection counter (D-32), and sends it in `params` alongside `v` / `sender` / `from`. Both sides log it on `channel-request` / `channel-response`. It is wire-safe under arch Mixed-version tolerance, because readers skip unknown fields. A server receiving a frame without `conn` from an older peer logs `srv_conn = "srv-<accept counter>"` instead, and so does a server receiving a `conn` outside the shape `^[a-z]+-\d+-\d+-\d+$` or over 64 bytes (a peer-supplied value is logged only in that shape). The server strips `conn` from `params` before dispatch: it is never an input to a method.
  - **Join key.** The merged-log join key for channel lines is `(conn, corr)`, and `instance` is deliberately **not** part of it (D-25).
    - `conn` is unique across the session home (`<process>-<pid>-<t0>-<n>`, D-10, D-32). `<pid>` alone is not unique: PIDs are recycled. Every `hook` process opens exactly one connection (`n` = 1) and sends the same first JSON-RPC `id`, so without `t0` two hook calls from a reused PID would share `(conn, corr)`.
    - Each side logs its **own** instance. `cli` and `mcp` log the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`, which is also `from`. `run` logs the wrapper's `ViolaName`. So the two sides of one call carry different `instance` values.
    - `srv_conn` lines from older peers have no client-side counterpart. They join only within the server's own file.
  - **`cli` instance precedence** (init step 3): the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` comes first. The explicit target `ViolaName` argument becomes `instance`, and names the `cli-<name>.ndjson` file, only when `VIOLA_NAME` is unset. So `viola send --to B` run by driver A logs `instance:"A"` to `cli-A.ndjson`.
  - `agent-run logs --instance B` therefore shows only B's side of a call. To reach the caller, take `conn` from B's `channel-request` and query with no `--instance` filter, for example `agent-run logs | jq -c 'select(.record.conn=="cli-4812-1790219525118-1")'`.
  - **Send cursor on early refusals.** The arch `send` result returns `cursor` only on success or `unconfirmable`; a refusal result carries `refusal` + `detail` only. For a send refused before `send-issued` (`human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `input-not-ready`, `turn-running`), the wrapper's `send-refused` carries `corr` = the target's `events.ndjson` end offset at the moment of refusal. This value is a log join key only. It is never returned to the caller and is not a `wait after` value. After `send-issued`, every `send-*` line carries the issued cursor. The cursor alone is not a unique send key. Refusals at an unchanged end offset can share it, and a later issued send can reuse it.
  - **Send ↔ channel link (D-30).** Every wrapper `send-*` line also carries `conn` (or `srv_conn` for an older peer) and `rpc_id`, the JSON-RPC `id` of the `send` request it answers. The pair `(conn, rpc_id)` on a send line equals `(conn, corr)` on that call's `channel-request` / `channel-response`, on both sides. So the caller reaches the wrapper's send lines, and the wrapper's send lines reach the caller, without timestamp guessing. One send is identified by target `instance` + `corr` + `conn` + `rpc_id`.
  - `from` is logged with the constant companion `from_trust:"self-reported"` and is never treated as identity.
  - JSON-RPC notifications (`hook.event`) have no `id`, so their `channel-request` has a null `corr`. They join through `hook_event` + `instance` + `timestamp`.

- **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs, so no file is both appended to and exclusively locked (a layout chosen while Windows, where that pair fails (rust-lang/rust#54118), was a target, and kept). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

This requires exit 0 and a last stdout line matching `^stamped \S+  \d+ pass  0 fail$`. It is the only writer of `ledger/stamps.json`; see Decisions Log.
  5. Spawn the supervisor `viola-harness supervise --session <id>` as an ordinary child process (no detach flags; it outlives `boot` and stops only through `stop.request`). It owns one portable-pty (`=0.8.1`, via the `viola-pty` seam) outer PTY per instance — a master writer, the child and a drain thread — and runs `viola run <name> --home <home> -- <bin dir>/viola-fake-agent --cli-version <ver> --fixtures <workspace root>/fixtures/claude --receipt <home>/fake/<name>.receipt.ndjson --control <home>/fake/<name>.control --screens --trusted-root <cwd> <fake-agent-args>`, so a booted wrapper shows the trusted ready screen, where `viola` is also taken from `<bin dir>`. `--fixtures` names the parent dir: the fake agent joins `<cli-version>` itself, so replay follows `--cli-version` even under `--report-version`. `--plugin-dir` is not passed by the harness: `viola run` passes it to the child (architecture §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names). It drains every master on its own thread. `<bin dir>` is the directory boot step 3 copies from: `target/harness/debug` (boot step 1's target dir) for the CLI, the test executable's own target dir for `harness_session`, and `target/perf/release` for `--perf`. The harness never reads `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`, because Cargo sets that only for the root package's own integration tests. `<workspace root>` is resolved from `cargo metadata` or `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` and passed as an absolute path, because nextest runs `viola-e2e` tests with `crates/viola-e2e` as the cwd. The control file is created empty before spawn. Both rstest `booted_wrapper` copies pass the same `--control` path.

- Output format: `{"v":1,"cmd":"run","ok":<bool>,"suites":[{"suite":"nextest-unit"|"nextest-integration"|"doctest"|"nextest-e2e"|"mutants"|"coverage"|"perf"|"fuzz-replay"|"local-live","passed":n,"failed":n,"skipped":n,"survived":n,"artifact":"<path>"}]}`.
  - Built from `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`, `mutants.out/outcomes.json` (the run's own output dir; `survived` = missed − host-excluded + timeout, step 4 Verdict; read only on the `counted`, `scoped` and `package` verdicts), `cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only`, and the hyperfine `--export-json` files.
  - A `--mutants` run adds a top-level `mutants` object: `{"tested":N,"verdict":"counted","base":"<sha>"}`, or `{"tested":0,"verdict":"no-rust-delta","base":"<sha>","diff":"target/agent-run/chunk.diff","files":N}` when the chunk diff names no `.rs` path, or `{"tested":0,"verdict":"test-only-rust-delta","base":"<sha>","diff":"target/agent-run/chunk.diff","files":N,"rust_files":[<repo-relative .rs paths>]}` when every `.rs` path is a test target (step 4; `rust_files` appears on that verdict only). `base` is the full sha of the base the run read (a commit id, never a path), so every run of a pass can be shown to read the same chunk. With `--file` the object is `{"tested":N,"verdict":"scoped","base":"<sha>","files":[<the given paths>]}`: survivors stay red as in a counted run. With `--package` it is `{"tested":N,"verdict":"package","package":"<member>"}` (no `base`, no `diff`), plus `"files"` when `--file` was given. A counted, scoped or package object also carries `"host_excluded"` when at least one mutant was left out (step 4, Verdict): an array of `{"name","cfg"}`, the name cargo-mutants' own and the predicate as written in source, repo-relative and never an absolute path. The field is absent when nothing was left out.
  - The run document gains a top-level `"archived"` (after `mutants` in key order) whenever the run had a source to archive: the repo-relative `target/run-archive/<n>` holding the JUnit files this run's nextest or coverage suites wrote (`junit-{nextest-unit,nextest-integration,coverage}.xml`) and the `outcomes.json` its mutation arm read (`<n>` = the highest existing + 1; the newest 10 kept; gitignored, outside `target/agent-run/`, never uploaded). An absent source is skipped and named on stderr (`run-archive: skipped {name} (absent)`).
  - A document refused by a tool arm carries `"reason"` and, where one applies, `"detail"` (e.g. `tool-missing` + `cargo-fuzz`).
  - `skipped` counts only tests that were selected and then not run: JUnit `<skipped/>` entries (`#[ignore]`). Tests excluded by the layer filterset (for example `kind(test)` binaries during `nextest-unit`) and tests compiled out by an OS `#[cfg(…)]` gate are never counted, so the `gate` `suite-skipped` breach fires only on a real skip. The `doctest` suite has no JUnit. It is counted from the `test result: … N passed; M failed; K ignored` lines of `cargo test --workspace --doc`, with `ignored` as `skipped`, so doc examples that must not run use `no_run` or a `text` fence, never `ignore`.
  - Failing test names are listed in `suites[].failures[]`.
- **Perf:** `agent-run run --perf` in its own `perf` job, its verdict from `viola-harness gate`, never from a `jq` binary.

5. **Verification:** the tests secret-scan test (`Cookie` header, `CLAUDE*` values, the content canary, 0600) over every `diagnostics/` file, run in CI before artifact upload.
   - **High classes** (prompt and send text, `last_assistant_message`, tool `input`, dialog answers, drift-report echoes):
     - Every E2E and integration input is synthetic and embeds a fixed canary string.
     - The scan also asserts that the canary never appears in a home-level `diagnostics/*.ndjson`. It may appear only in `detail-*.ndjson`.
     - The `mcp_tools` E2E case `mcp_tools_a_line_past_max_frame_ends_the_session_with_one_line` runs on its own fresh home, writes the canary inside its over-long stdin line, and asserts the canary in no home-level file of that home.
     - The canary value and the test body are tests-owned.
   - **Detail-file upload** (§9) is admissible only because every input is synthetic. It covers two artifacts: the `test` job's `diag-<os>` and the `perf` job's `diag-perf-<os>` (`target/e2e-home/**/diagnostics/*.ndjson`), whose inputs are the per-row synthetic hook payloads (string fields, the tests-owned canary in content fields) and the `fake-agent` seam's fixed ASCII panic payload (in `detail-hook.ndjson` only; the home-level `panic` line stays payload-free). The same job's `perf-<os>` (hyperfine timings and repo-relative command lines only) and `diag-perf-<os>` upload only when `always() && steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'` — the same channel, scan gate and synthetic-input basis as `diag-<os>`, not a new crossing.
   - The same rule covers the `harness-<os>` artifact. `agent-run logs` merges `events.ndjson` records (`prompt-submitted.data.text`, `last_assistant_message`) and detail lines, so it carries the canary by design. The scan applies the Critical-class patterns to `target/agent-run/*` except exactly `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, and the canary rule exempts those files as it exempts `detail-*.ndjson`. That one file is `run --mutants`' diff, repository source text by construction (it hits the scan's own Critical-class patterns whenever it touches them); the `harness-<os>` upload excludes it (`!target/agent-run/chunk.diff`), so it is never scanned and never uploaded. A `chunk.diff` anywhere else under the capture is still scanned.
   - Any non-synthetic input source must first drop `detail-*.ndjson` and `target/agent-run/` from the upload paths.
   - The local `viola-harness pre-push` document is never uploaded and carries no absolute path, only codes and counts. The gate runs natively on the Linux host in the working tree itself (no clone), so neither the repository root nor the passwd home (`<home>`, `<home>/.cargo/bin`) reaches it. `pre_push_document_carries_no_absolute_path` asserts it, red at the Linux tests and green (chunks 2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate and 2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion).
   - A server-verification refusal carries no pid, start time, path or endpoint: `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` scans every output and the `cli-<name>.ndjson` line with `digit_runs` (whole numbers only, itself tested by `digit_runs_reads_whole_numbers_only`), on Linux.
   - A strict-modes refusal of the six frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, through `client::refuse_untrusted`) carries no pid, path or endpoint and writes no line: it prints only the fixed instance pair, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`; `tests/security_negatives_strict_modes.rs` reads every output with `digit_runs` and finds no line, on Linux. The `viola mcp` frame tools refused by the same check return `instance-unreachable` with `detail: "strict-modes-failed"` and write no line (`binary(handlers)`).
   - A socket-directory refusal carries no path, pid or uid in its lines and documents, and its human pair names only the parsed `ViolaName`: `tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs` reads them with `assert_names_nothing` and `digit_runs`, on Linux.
   - **Error-body census:** `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` (`andromeda:walks-tree`) holds the error bodies of CLI `--json`, MCP results and the seven channel faults in tables: `error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand` holds each body to a writer and a witness that stand, `product_error_writers_are_each_named` holds every product error writer to a name, and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` holds `thiserror` messages free of interpolation.
   - **Error-body check:** `tests/support/events.rs` holds `error_body_hit` and `assert_error_body_clean`, classes `absolute-path`, `caused-by`, `serde-path` and `planted`, reporting place and class, never bytes. No check runs after every test: the four live witnesses, the enumeration and the census read it instead. It stands beside the secret scan and leaves the scan as it is.
   - **Live witnesses of clean error bodies:** `channel_error_bodies_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` (`tests/channel_error_bodies.rs`), `cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` and `cli_error_documents_of_a_loosened_socket_directory_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` (`tests/cli_error_bodies.rs`) and `mcp_tools_error_results_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`).
   - The content sink is opened only behind its strict-modes check: `src/obs.rs`'s `check_diagnostics` runs `viola_state::strict::check_diagnostics` on the `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or `detail-<process>.ndjson` file, each that exists, in `open_role_file` and `write_detail`, before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything. A symlink, a folder another user may read (a group or other bit) or a file another user may read (a group or other bit) refuses the open as a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink` and the detail line is dropped, so High-class content is never written through a symlink or into a folder another user may read (unit cases in `src/obs.rs`).
   - **Unscanned uploads, admissible by content** (operator ratification 2026-09-24):
     - (the CI mutants legs' `mutants-verdict-<os>.json` left with those jobs on 2026-09-28.) `mutants.out/` is never uploaded (its `outcomes.json` held absolute argv paths; its `log/` held test output). On the Linux dev host a directory named `viola-mutants-scratch/` is only the operator's NOCOW `TMPDIR` for cargo-mutants' copy trees — an environment fact, not harness code — and no document prints it either; `mutants.out/` there stays at the repository root (gitignored). `target/run-archive/<n>/`, where each `run` copies the JUnit files it wrote and the `outcomes.json` it read, is never uploaded either: gitignored and outside `target/agent-run/` and every other upload path; the run document names it only by the repo-relative `archived`.
     - the nightly `fuzz` job's `fuzz/artifacts/` (on `failure()`) holds crash inputs the fuzzer mutated from the committed synthetic `fuzz/corpus/<target>/`. A non-synthetic corpus seed must first drop that upload.
     - the ci.yml `supply-chain` artifact (`target/supply-chain/deny.json`, `deny-fuzz.json` for the `fuzz/Cargo.lock` audit, and `zizmor.json`; `if: always()`, 7 days) holds cargo-deny and zizmor diagnostics only: crate names and versions, advisory ids, registry URLs and workflow-relative locations. It carries no absolute path, argv, log content or user input (as measured at chunk 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes: 0 absolute paths in all three files; the one raw pattern hit was the `s:/` inside `https://`). The guard stays binding: a member that could carry a host path or log content is scanned before upload, or dropped (operator ratification 2026-09-24, logged for founder review).
   - **Scan failure:**
     - The pre-upload ban wins: no `diag-<os>` or `harness-<os>` artifact is uploaded in the `test` job, and no `perf-<os>` or `diag-perf-<os>` in the `perf` job; that job's hit report uploads as `secret-scan-perf-<os>`.
     - Instead, the scan step writes a hit report to `target/secret-scan/` (`file`, line, byte offset and pattern class, never the matched bytes), and the separate §9 step 5 uploads that directory as `secret-scan-${{ matrix.os }}`.
     - So the failing job still leaves agent-readable evidence (§11 CI).

| hyperfine `--export-json target/agent-run/artifacts/perf-<hook>.json`, one per row (`session-start`, `user-prompt-submit`, `stop`, `session-end`, `pre-tool-use`), from `run --perf` in the `perf` job | `if: always() && steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'`, so a failing gate still leaves its samples and a failed scan withholds them (timings and repo-relative benchmarked command lines only, no log content) | uploaded as `perf-${{ matrix.os }}`, with the same job's home diagnostics as `diag-perf-${{ matrix.os }}` under the same condition | `jq '.results[0].max'` |

1. Integration and E2E tests (every viola home under `target/e2e-home/` but the one `viola-chaos-*` home of `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs`, outside G2, G4 and the secret scan by the founder's ruling of 2026-10-04), then G2 and G4, **both** `if: always()`. The hyperfine perf gates do not run in the `test` job: they run in their own `perf` job (`fail-fast: false`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`), whose steps are `run --perf`, G2 (probe then check), `schema-check` and `secret-scan`, all `if: always()`, the scan-gated `perf-<os>` and `diag-perf-<os>` uploads, `secret-scan-perf-<os>` on a scan failure, and last `gate --require perf`. So G2, G4 and the scan cover the perf home under that job's own artifact names, with no `diag-<os>` collision. A failed test step must not skip G2: failing runs are where panic lines are most likely, and §10 measures panics only through G2's exit code (D-29). **Homes are kept until the gate steps have run** (overseer fix pass 2, B1): `ci.yml` sets `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, so neither harness `cleanup` nor a test home's drop deletes a home before G2, G4, the secret scan and the scan-gated uploads have read it (test-plan §3 `cleanup` step 6). Without it, a green run leaves `target/e2e-home/` empty, G2's non-empty check fails, and nothing is scanned.

- Boundary review:
  - `cargo modules orphans --deny` is a CI gate. `scripts/orphans-check.sh` runs it in the `lint` job once per lib/bin target from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, with `--features` for a target's required features (`viola-fake-agent`), and its `--probe` mode proves it fires on each of its two planted orphans first.
  - The `cargo modules dependencies` graph (`--acyclic`) stays an on-demand review, never a gate: cargo-modules 0.27.0 reports every type and its own inherent method as a cycle, whatever the filters (measured at the same chunk, 3 of 4 targets).
  - The rmcp release-graph check is `scripts/rmcp-features.sh` (landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): `cargo tree -e features -p viola --edges normal --target all -i rmcp --no-dedupe --prefix depth`; rmcp must be present (`rmcp-features: FAILED — rmcp is absent from viola's release graph`), and the features a non-rmcp package requests must be exactly `server transport-io`; verdict `rmcp-features: server transport-io`. It runs in CI's `lint` job after `Lint probes`.

- The `release` job builds `cargo build --release --locked --bin viola` through `scripts/release-check.sh`. The script judges that build's own `compiler-artifact` records, never a `target/release/` listing. It refuses any executable other than `viola`, and any artifact whose `features` include a test-only feature (`test-support`, `fake-agent`): `release-check: FAILED — test-only feature {feature} in {target}`. `--probe` runs first and must read 5/5 refused with a clean control. `viola-channel`'s test-only `test-support` feature (shared test helpers) is enabled only by the root package's `[dev-dependencies]`.

- The `perf` job (job-level `contents: read`) installs hyperfine with `cargo install --locked hyperfine@1.20.0` as its own step (no new action, no `github.event` value) and runs `agent-run run --perf`, then G2, G4 and its own `secret-scan`. Its uploads `perf-<os>` (hyperfine exports) and `diag-perf-<os>` (the perf home's diagnostics) go up only when that scan succeeds, and `secret-scan-perf-<os>` only when it fails; every input is synthetic (obs-plan §8 item 6).

- The `viola` root bin's test-only Windows dev-dependency: windows-sys (the workspace pin `=0.61.2`) under `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dev-dependencies]`, with both features `Wdk_Storage_FileSystem` and `Win32_System_IO` (`NtQueryInformationFile` and its `IO_STATUS_BLOCK` argument need both), for the pipe-type read-back of `tests/security_negatives_channel.rs`. Both features already reach the Windows graph by unification (mio, interprocess, socket2), so `Cargo.lock` does not move, and under `resolver = "3"` no release build carries them.
